# United Future — track record (2008–2017 support agreements)

United Future never had more than one MP after 2008, so its "promises" that could actually be delivered were the
policy items it negotiated into its confidence-and-supply agreements with National. This page compares those written
commitments with what happened. Structured data: [`data/promises/united-future.json`](../../data/promises/united-future.json).

**How to read this:** only items with a source showing the outcome are given a status. Items we could not verify are
listed as *not verified* rather than guessed. The agreements themselves are primary sources (copies hosted by the
McGuinness Institute; local copies in `raw/minor-parties/agreements/`). [A1][A2][A3]

## What United Future gave

- Confidence and supply to National-led governments for three full terms (2008–2017), plus support on procedural
  motions. There is no record in our sources of Dunne withdrawing confidence. [A1][A2][A3]
- In the 2011–14 term the government's majority was thin and Dunne "held the balance of power for more than ten pieces
  of legislation", including the asset-sales (mixed-ownership) programme, which he supported subject to his 49% cap. [S1]

## 2008 agreement (Dated 14 November 2008) [A1]

| Commitment | Outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Dunne Minister of Revenue and Associate Minister of Health, outside Cabinet | Appointed and held both until his June 2013 resignation [S1] | kept |
| Support United Future's income-splitting legislation to first reading | Taxation (Income-sharing Tax Credit) Bill passed first reading 64–54 in September 2010 [S2][S1] | kept |
| Establish a Big Game Hunting Council, with a view to a statutory body | Government announced a Game Animal Council in 2011; the Game Animal Council Bill was before Parliament in 2012 [S1][S3] (see 2011 item) | kept |
| Support PPPs for major roads such as Transmission Gully | Transmission Gully built as a public-private partnership; construction began 8 Sept 2014 [S4] | kept |
| Keep the Families Commission's policy/research/advocacy role | Commission retained, then restructured (see 2011) [S5] | partially-kept |
| Reduce elective-surgery waiting lists using private capacity; progress Medicines NZ strategy | not verified | — |

## 2011 agreement [A2]

| Commitment | Outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|
| No sale of any part of Kiwibank or Radio New Zealand | Both remained wholly state-owned; Kiwibank is still state-owned in 2026 [S6][S7] | kept |
| Statutory cap: no more than 49% of shares in public assets sold to private interests | The mixed-ownership model sold down Genesis, Meridian and Mighty River Power from 100% to 51% and Air NZ from 74% to 51%; Solid Energy's sale was dropped [S8] | kept |
| Pass the Game Animal Council legislation to make the Council a statutory body | The Council became a statutory body (Game Animal Council Act 2013 — Act title from general knowledge; legislation.govt.nz could not be fetched) [S3] | kept |
| Reinstate the Income Sharing Bill | Reinstated, but it "never had a second reading" [S1] | partially-kept |
| Government discussion document on "Flexi-Super" (choose NZ Super start age 60–70) | Discussion document released by Finance Minister Bill English in August 2013; Treasury later advised against proceeding and the policy was not adopted [S9] | kept (document) / not adopted (policy) |
| Restructure the Families Commission (single commissioner, new monitoring/evaluation role, Families Status Report, $4m for parenting programmes) | Families Commission Amendment Act 2014 (third reading 24 March 2014, 64–56) created Superu with a stronger research function [S5] | kept |
| PPPs for major roading, "in particular the Transmission Gully highway" | PPP contract; construction from 2014, opened 2022 (late and over budget) [S4] | kept |
| Maintain at least current Budget funding tracks for TVNZ and RNZ | not verified in this pass (RNZ's funding level over 2011–14 not sourced) | — |
| Investigate a free annual health check for over-65s "when fiscal circumstances allow" | No evidence it was implemented | not verified |
| End guided helicopter hunting/herding on the conservation estate; youth one-stop shops; pre-release AOD assessments for prisoners; free public access to rivers/lakes/coast | not verified | — |
| Dunne Minister of Revenue, Associate Health, Associate Conservation | Appointed; resigned 7 June 2013 over the GCSB-report email inquiry, reinstated (as Internal Affairs, Associate Health, Associate Conservation) 28 Jan 2014 [S1] | kept |

## 2014 agreement (Dated 29 September 2014) [A3]

The 2014 agreement was much thinner: United Future's "priorities to progress" rather than firm commitments.

| Priority | Outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Dunne Minister of Internal Affairs, Associate Health, Associate Conservation (outside Cabinet) | Appointed and served to 2017. As Internal Affairs minister he extended passports to 10 years and led creation of Fire and Emergency New Zealand [S1] | kept |
| Next iteration of the Medicines NZ strategy; enhanced role for pharmacists | not verified | — |
| Improve water quality in lakes, rivers and streams | not verified (no measurable commitment) | — |
| Recreational fishers — National's recreational fishing parks policy | not verified | — |
| Re-affirm PPPs for major roading where appropriate | Transmission Gully PPP proceeded [S4] | kept |
| Flexible superannuation (sought by UF) | Not included in the 2014 deal [S10] | — |

## Other actions in office (not in the agreements)

- **Psychoactive Substances Act 2013:** Dunne, as Associate Health Minister responsible for drugs, introduced the
  regulated market for "legal highs"; in 2015–17 he moved to make cannabis-based medicines more available. [S1][S11]
- **2013 resignation:** Dunne refused to hand over emails with a journalist to the inquiry into the leaked GCSB report
  and resigned; the Privileges Committee later found he was within his rights. [S1]

## Assessment

On the items that can be checked, United Future's record of getting its negotiated items implemented is strong:
the "no sale" of Kiwibank/RNZ, the 49% cap, the Game Animal Council, the Families Commission changes and the
Transmission Gully PPP all happened. Its two signature tax/retirement policies — income splitting and flexi-super —
got only procedural wins (a first reading; a discussion document) and were never enacted. Critics argued its
influence depended on National's tolerance in Ōhāriu rather than voter support (0.2–0.6% of the party vote). [S1][A2]

Wasted-vote figures for 2011–2020 match the "below electoral threshold" rows in the official summaries; the 2023 figure
(159,043 of 2,884,111 party votes) is computed the same way. The wasted vote in 2008 was 6.5%. Effective number of
parties = 1/Σ(vote share²), computed by `tools/minor_parties_overview.py`. [1][4]

## Trends

### 1. A crowded ballot, but the same small club in Parliament
The number of registered parties on the ballot rose from 13 (2011) to 17 (2020, 2023, 2026), yet the number winning
seats fell from eight to five or six. Every party that won seats from 2017 on was one of the "big six". The two minor
parties that held seats in 2011–14 — United Future and Mana — did so only through a single electorate seat, and both
lost it (Dunne retired in 2017; Harawira was beaten in 2014 after National and NZ First leaders encouraged tactical
votes for Labour's Kelvin Davis). [1][5][6]

### 2. The 5% threshold and the electorate "lifeboat"
Under MMP a party needs 5% of the party vote **or** one electorate seat. In this period no new party crossed 5%; the
closest were the Conservatives (3.97% in 2014) and TOP (2.44% in 2017). The electorate route explains every minor-party
MP: Ōhāriu (United Future, helped by National's low-key campaigns there, which Labour called an "unprincipled political
deal"), Te Tai Tokerau (Mana), and — for the big six — Epsom (ACT) and the Māori seats (Te Pāti Māori, which won six
seats in 2023 on 3.08%). Small parties therefore chase winnable electorates: Colin Craig's hoped-for accommodation on
the North Shore (refused by John Key in 2014), TOP's Ōhāriu (2020) and Ilam (2023, Raf Manji second by 7,830 votes),
DemocracyNZ's Northland (2023) and Te Tai Tokerau Party's bid in 2026. [5][7][8][9]

The Independent Electoral Review (final report November 2023) examined the threshold and the one-electorate rule; its
report could not be re-fetched for this page, so its recommendations are not summarised here. No threshold change was
made for 2026: the Electoral Amendment Act 2025 dealt with enrolment deadlines, prisoner voting, donation disclosure
thresholds and conduct near polling places. [10]

### 3. "Wasted" votes peaked in 2020
The share of party votes for parties winning no seat nearly doubled from 3.3% (2011) to 6.1% (2014) as the Conservatives
and Internet MANA both missed out, and peaked at **7.7% in 2020**, when NZ First (2.60%) fell out of Parliament alongside
TOP (1.51%), New Conservative (1.48%) and Advance NZ (0.98%). Because these votes are excluded before seats are
allocated, Labour won an outright majority (65 of 120 seats) on 50.0% of the vote. In 2023 it fell to 5.5%. [1][4]

### 4. The COVID-era protest vote, 2020–2023
2020 and 2023 saw a wave of anti-lockdown, anti-mandate and conspiracy-tinged parties:

| Election | Parties (party vote %) | Combined |
|---|---|---|
| 2020 | Advance NZ (with NZ Public Party) 0.98, Outdoors 0.11 | ≈1.1% |
| 2023 | NZ Loyal 1.21, Freedoms NZ (Vision NZ + Outdoors & Freedom) 0.34, DemocracyNZ 0.24, New Nation 0.05 | ≈1.8% |

(Grouping is this archive's; parties such as ONE/NewZeal, New Conservatives and the Leighton Baker Party overlapped with
this movement on some issues but are counted separately.) The movement fragmented rather than consolidated: Freedoms NZ
failed to bring in DemocracyNZ or the Leighton Baker Party, DemocracyNZ lost candidates and donors to NZ First, and NZ
Loyal split between Liz Gunn and Kelvyn Alp. Seven parties deregistered between the 2023 and 2026 elections — DemocracyNZ,
Leighton Baker Party, NZ Loyal (since re-registered), Democratic Alliance, New Nation, Freedoms NZ and NewZeal — and
NewZeal's leader Alfred Ngaro joined NZ First, which itself returned to Parliament in 2023 with 6.09%. [11][12][13][2]

### 5. The Christian-conservative lane
Christian and socially conservative parties have repeatedly split their vote: in 2020 New Conservative (1.48%), ONE
(0.28%) and Vision NZ (0.15%) together took ≈1.9%; in 2023 NewZeal (0.57%), New Conservatives (0.16%), the Leighton Baker
Party (0.07%) and Vision NZ (inside Freedoms NZ) again fell far short. [1][14]

### 6. The durable fringe
Some parties persist regardless of results: the Legalise Cannabis Party has polled 0.31–0.52% at every election since
2011; Social Credit stood until its leader's death in 2023; the Alliance re-registered in 2026 after an 11-year gap with
the backing of the Maritime Union. [15][16]

## 2026 outlook

- **17 registered parties** are contesting the party vote: the six parliamentary parties plus Alliance, Animal Justice,
  Legalise Cannabis, Conservative Party NZ, Free Palestine, NZ Loyal, Opportunity, NZ Outdoors & Freedom, Te Tai Tokerau,
  Vision NZ and Women's Rights. Three (Free Palestine, Te Tai Tokerau Party and NZ Loyal) were registered on 5 August
  2026, the same day the Alliance's re-registration took effect. [2][3]
- **Opportunity (TOP)** is the only minor party with a realistic chance of crossing 5%: it peaked at 9.5% (Roy Morgan,
  August) and polled 4.8–8% in October 2026, qualified for TVNZ's multi-party debate, and has been ruled out as a partner
  by National (27 July). See the [TOP profile](opportunity/README.md). [17][18]
- **Te Tai Tokerau Party** could win a seat through the electorate route if Kapa-Kingi holds Te Tai Tokerau. [19]
- Broadcasting money: of the minor parties, Opportunity received the largest allocation ($118,755 amended), then NZ
  Loyal ($86,306); "Change New Zealand" and "People's Party NZ Inc." were provisionally allocated $78,887 each but did not
  register and received nothing. [2]

# ACT New Zealand — 2026 election policies

Every 2026 general-election (7 November 2026) policy of ACT New Zealand that this archive could find: **110 policies** — 91 from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz/parties/act-party) and 19 additional policies found only on [act.org.nz](https://www.act.org.nz/policies) — backed by **128 full-text source documents** (54 policy page, 31 policy document (PDF), 27 press release, 14 policy index page, 1 press release (Scoop mirror), 1 fiscal plan microsite).

**How this was built** ([`tools/policies_act_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_act_fetch.py), [`tools/policies_act_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_act_build.py)):

- Starting point: the policy.nz dataset for ACT (`raw/policy.nz/parties/act-party.json`, 91 statements; policy.nz citations were accessed between 06 August 2026 and 19 October 2026). The **Why / How** text for those entries is policy.nz's neutral summary ("This party says …"), reproduced unchanged.
- Every cited source was fetched again directly from its origin (policy.nz cites Wayback Machine snapshots; the archived original URL was fetched instead) on 2026-10-23. HTML pages were reduced to their main content; PDFs were converted with `pdftotext` (designed multi-column PDFs can interleave sidebars with body text in reading order; the original PDFs are kept in `raw/party-docs/act/pdf/`).
- The full act.org.nz sitemap was crawled for policy pages (`/policies/*` index pages plus every policy landing page, excluding people, news archive and "ACT's Record" pages, which describe past actions rather than 2026 commitments). Every "Read the full policy" PDF linked from those pages was downloaded too.
- Policies on act.org.nz that policy.nz does not list were added with `summary_source: "archive"` (IDs `ACT-A01`…`ACT-A19`); their Why/How summaries were written for this archive from the linked ACT page and should be checked against the full text.
- Each policy links to the full verbatim text of its sources in [`documents/`](documents/). Duplicate PDFs (same file at several URLs) are stored once, with all URLs listed in the front matter.
- Structured data: [`policies.json`](policies.json).

> Summaries describe what ACT says it would do; they are not endorsements or fact-checks. ACT's own claims (costs, statistics) are reported as ACT's claims.

ACT's own [Fiscal Plan page](documents/fiscalplan.md) summarises its programme as (verbatim):

- Balance the books with no new taxes, putting much lower taxes within reach.
- Cut $9.5 billion a year from spending outside welfare and protected frontline services once fully implemented.
- Make government smaller and more accountable, with 19 departments and 18 ministers responsible for budgets and results.
- Remove tax on KiwiSaver investment earnings and discontinue the government contribution.
- Introduce a Carbon Tax Refund, returning net revenue from Emissions Trading Scheme auctions to New Zealanders.
- Gradually raise the NZ Super age to 67 by 2035, with compassionate early access for people who have spent much of their careers in physically demanding jobs.

## Fiscal plan / alternative budget

ACT released its **[ACT Fiscal Plan 2026](documents/pdf-act-2026-fiscal-plan.md)** (12-page PDF, 11 October 2026; [original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/38747/attachments/original/1791599898/ACT_2026_Fiscal_Plan.pdf?1791599898)), with a landing page ([fiscalplan](documents/fiscalplan.md)) and an interactive debt microsite ([balancethebooks.nz](documents/fiscal-plan.md)). Key figures as stated in the PDF (all figures are ACT's; $ nominal):

- **Debt:** net core Crown debt (excluding NZ Super Fund) of $217 billion by June 2031, which ACT says is $12.4 billion lower than current Treasury forecasts (the PDF's "Headline Figures" page also describes it as "$12 billion lower than forecast in the Pre-election Fiscal Update"; the costing table shows 217.336 vs 229.769).
- **Operating balance:** OBEGAL surplus of $13.6 billion in 2030/31 (vs $8.9 billion under current Government plans); OBEGALx $16.4 billion (vs $11.7 billion); OBEGALx in small surplus in 2027/28, a year earlier than current plans; OBEGAL returns to a $5.1 billion surplus in 2028/29.
- **No new taxes; no broad-based tax cuts in this plan** — "several strategic tax cuts" instead: no tax on KiwiSaver earnings ($1.065bn in 2027/28 rising to $1.437bn in 2030/31), a Carbon Tax Refund (est. ~$100 per household), an uncapped donation tax credit, reformed crypto tax treatment, and $264m of targeted tax relief "to be announced".
- **New operating spending (outside the operating allowance), $445m in 2027/28 rising to $551m:** expanded pharmacy minor-ailments scheme, Local Tourism Dividend, Young Investors Fund (~$35m/yr, $500 for Year 11 students), Overstayers Investigation Unit ($60m/yr), rural crime funding, electronic money management for long-term Jobseeker recipients, Three Strikes for Burglary, Working with Children Check, independent school subsidy indexation, and a $100m/yr initiative "to be announced".
- **Savings:** future operating allowances cut from $2.4bn to $2bn a year (+$0.4bn in 2027/28 rising to +$1.6bn in 2030/31); non-welfare, non-frontline spending returned to 2017 levels per person (headline reductions $1.5bn in 2027/28, $2.8bn, $3.2bn, $2.4bn in 2030/31 — including abolishing demographic ministries ~$187m/yr and cutting foreign aid to 2017 levels excluding Ukraine ~$283m/yr); NZ Super age rising by three months a year to 67 by 2035 ($0.46bn rising to $1.89bn, less compassionate early access); five-year benefit stand-down for residence-class visa holders; tighter medical certification for health/disability benefits; replacing the KiwiSaver Government Contribution ($0.52–0.59bn/yr); lower financing costs ($452m by 2030/31).
- **Capital/non-operating:** $2m for anti-social noise cameras; $2bn contingency for a National Cancer Centre; $150m contingency for a new Epsom secondary school; maintain the suspension of NZ Super Fund contributions.
- The landing page states ACT would "Cut $9.5 billion a year from spending outside welfare and protected frontline services once fully implemented" and "Make government smaller and more accountable, with 19 departments and 18 ministers".

## Community & inclusion

### Make the abuse of a companion animal in a family violence situation a crime (POL54651)

***Key policy** (policy.nz) · Topics: community-and-inclusion, law-justice-and-government, animal-welfare, women, family-justice-and-safety, key-policies-community-and-inclusion · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Make the abuse of a companion animal in a family violence situation a crime

**Why:** This party says that pets are being threatened and abused to coerce people in family violence situations and prevent them from leaving. Research shows half of victims delay leaving a violent situation because they are concerned about their pets. Criminalising the abuse of animals in this context will give Police more tools to protect victims. States in Australia and the US have enacted similar laws and New Zealand needs to do the same.

**How:** This party would amend the Crimes Act to make abusing a pet with the goal of coercion an offence punishable by a maximum seven years in prison. Protection orders would be strengthened to ensure offenders cannot control access to a pet and ensure pets are not left with abusers. Police would be required to record the presence of pets in a family violence situation and receive clear operational guidance around removing pets to a safe place if the animal is at risk of harm.

### Remove the carbon price floor and return ETS profits to households (POL55047)

***Key policy** (policy.nz) · Topics: environment, economy, incomes-and-employment, emissions-reduction, government-revenue-and-finance, prices, key-policies-economy · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Remove the carbon price floor and return ETS profits to households

**Why:** This party says that the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS) acts as a "carbon tax", with a minimum price for carbon credits set by the government. This means the auctions do not work properly and raises the price of goods and services. The supply of carbon credits should be increased and the profit returned as a refund to New Zealanders.

**How:** This party would remove the price floor from the Emissions Trading Scheme to place downward pressure on the carbon price. 100 percent of the money from the carbon auction would be returned to New Zealanders as a tax refund. If the amount became so low that the refund was impractical to deliver, it would mean prices had fallen so that people had lower prices for goods and services and would no longer need the tax refund.  Conversions of farmland to permanent forest for creating carbon credits would be discouraged.

### Count carbon dioxide and methane differently under emissions targets (POL54667)

*Topics: environment, economy, emissions-reduction, agriculture, climate-adaptation · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Count carbon dioxide and methane differently under emissions targets

**Why:** This party says that carbon dioxide and methane both contribute to global heating. Carbon dioxide stays in the atmosphere longer than methane, which is largely produced by the dairy and sheep industries.

**How:** This party would rewrite NZ's Nationally Determined Contributions plan, which is required by the Paris Agreement. It would differentiate between the emissions caused by methane and carbon dioxide so that methane emissions do not have to be reduced by the same degree as carbon emissions. A "split gas approach" would calculate the emissions generated by carbon dioxide and methane differently. Carbon dioxide emissions would be reduced while methane levels could continue at current levels.

### Introduce noise-detecting cameras (POL55159)

**Statement:** Introduce noise-detecting cameras

**Why:** This party says that neighborhoods are frustrated by loud vehicles late at night. It notes that families are woken up by loud noises and are stressed about how such noise affects their sleep or the sleep of young children.

**How:** This party would introduce noise-detecting cameras in place of present police officers. These cameras would feature microphones, video and number plate recognition. ### Exclude purely spiritual and religious effects from infrastructure planning law (POL55191)

*Topics: te-ao-maori, transport-and-infrastructure, te-reo-maori-and-culture, infrastructure-funding-and-planning · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Exclude purely spiritual and religious effects from infrastructure planning law

**Why:** This party says that spiritual beliefs, particularly those that come from Te Ao Māori, should not be used as the basis for assessing an infrastructure project's viability. It says that planning law should regulate effects that can be identified, measured and tested, and protect rights recognised by law. It should not require planners, councils or judges to rule on spiritual or religious beliefs.

**How:** This party would exclude purely spiritual and religious effects. It would legislate that a religious or spiritual belief, or a claim of spiritual harm, could not on its own be treated as an adverse effect or justify refusing or restricting consent, requesting further information, or imposing a consent condition. The rule would apply equally to all religions and belief systems and use the test already applied under the Marine and Coastal Area (Takutai Moana) Act. It would also ban compulsory spiritual observances. No consent or permit could require anyone to perform, take part in, arrange or fund a prayer, karakia, blessing or other religious observance. Anyone who wants to do these things voluntarily could still do so.

It would facilitate this by adding property rights into the New Zealand Bill of Rights Act and ensuring that any legal challenge opposing a permit does not suspend that permit.

### Create a set of national mineral extractions standards (POL55221)

*Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, te-ao-maori, economy, energy, urban-planning-and-resource-management, land-and-resources, oil-gas-and-mining · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Create a set of national mineral extractions standards

**Why:** This party says that New Zealand's economy would benefit from more jobs in resource and mineral extraction, and the government would gain from increased royalty payments.

**How:** This party would guarantee regular updates to the Crown Mineral List, establish national policy direction and standards for mines, quarries and mineral processing under the new planning legislation, retain fast-track access for eligible projects, and have government work alongside industry to build up the workforce in extractive industries.

**Full text:**

- ['Unlocking Mineral and Energy Wealth' (PDF), 8 October 2026 (accessed 08 October 2026)](documents/pdf-unlocking-mineral-and-energy-wealth.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/actnz/pages/38384/attachments/original/1791257386/Unlocking_Mineral_and_Energy_Wealth.pdf?1791257386))
- [Unlocking Mineral Wealth](documents/unlocking-mineral-wealth.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/unlocking-mineral-wealth)) *(related)*

### Expand domestic energy production (POL55222)

*Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, economy, te-ao-maori, energy, oil-gas-and-mining, economic-development-and-industry, land-and-resources, urban-planning-and-resource-management · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Expand domestic energy production

**Why:** This party says that global energy markets are becoming more competitive. Expanding domestic energy production could bring commercial and security benefits for New Zealand and allied nations.

**How:** This party would continue to allow offshore gas exploration. It would encourage businesses to use renewable energy or fossil fuels with no preference for either option. It would revise the Crown Minerals Act to create rules for underground gas storage . It would also provide insurance for LNG (gas) import infrastructure.

**Full text:**

- [Unlocking Mineral Wealth](documents/unlocking-mineral-wealth.md) ([original](https://www.act.org.nz/unlocking-mineral-wealth)) *(related)*

### Revise legislation for resource extraction (POL55223)

*Topics: transport-and-infrastructure, economy, te-ao-maori, energy, oil-gas-and-mining, land-and-resources, urban-planning-and-resource-management · Summary: policy.nz*

**Statement:** Revise legislation for resource extraction

**Why:** This party says that regulatory barriers can create increased costs for investors and firms engaged in mining and gas and oil extraction. Regulations that duplicate criteria that are already met waste time, money and state resources.

**How:** This party would have separate legislation around mining with the goal of minimising similar regulations. One piece of legislation would focus on the allocation of Crown-owned petroleum and minerals, another on the management of environmental effects and another on consenting processes.

*Topics: energy, prices, emissions-reduction · Summary: this archive (not on policy.nz)*

**Statement:** Legalise plug-in solar and implement the Solar Regulatory Review

**Why:** Part of ACT's electricity policy; ACT says red tape is limiting household solar.

**How:** Implement the recommendations of the Ministry for Regulation's Solar Regulatory Review, including legalising plug-in solar, and lift unnecessary limits on households exporting solar power.

# Alliance Party of Aotearoa New Zealand — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Alliance Party of Aotearoa New Zealand** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **27 policies** listed, backed by **37 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://allianceparty.nz/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 (re-registered; Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The relaunched Alliance (leader Victor Billot) released its 2026 platform as a series of policy announcements (September–October 2026), each with a full policy PDF: tax and costings, workers' rights, environment, health, transport, social security, gender equality, small business, justice, child poverty, housing, retirement, Te Tiriti and constitution, trade, public ownership, and foreign affairs and defence. All 17 PDFs and all policy posts are captured. The main commitments of each document are listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/alliance/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Only the tax package has a separate costing document. Policy PDFs were extracted with pdftotext (page numbers kept). Earlier 2026 posts responding to news are captured where they state policy (Universal Child Benefit, conference).

# Animal Justice Party Aotearoa New Zealand (AJP) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Animal Justice Party Aotearoa New Zealand (AJP)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **38 policies** listed, backed by **51 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://animaljustice.org.nz/>
- Registration: 16 August 2023 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Animal Justice Party publishes an Election 2026 Manifesto, a plain-language Policy Summary (ten campaign themes), a 2026 full policy platform PDF (~23,000 words), four policy packs, and 40+ individual policy pages, most with their own PDF. All were captured (web text via the WordPress API plus each linked PDF). The list below gives the ten summary themes (marked as headline policies) followed by each detailed policy page.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/animal-justice/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Some individual policy PDFs date from 2024–2025 (publication dates are in each document's front matter); the party presents them as current. PDF text extraction splits decorative drop-capitals onto their own line.

## Community & inclusion

### Recognise animals in law as sentient beings rather than property (AJP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says the property classification makes meaningful protection very hard.

**How** (*archive*): Write sentience into legislation with enforceable protections and end codes of practice that let industries sidestep the Animal Welfare Act.

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says welfare is overseen by MPI, the same ministry that promotes farm exports — a conflict of interest.

**How** (*archive*): Modelled on the Children's Commissioner, with funding for welfare research and accountability for enforcement agencies.

**Why** (*archive*): The AJP says 60% of dogs impounded in Auckland last year were killed rather than rehomed.

### Protect and restore natural habitats and design roads and cities to protect wildlife (AJP-33)

**How** (*archive*): Wildlife impact assessments in urban planning and road design; help wild animals facing natural threats where appropriate.

# Conservative Party NZ (Conservatives NZ) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Conservative Party NZ (Conservatives NZ)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **19 policies** listed, backed by **27 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://www.conservatives.nz/ (2026 campaign site: https://conservatives.org.nz/)>
- Registration: 6 October 2011 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Conservative Party NZ (called the New Conservatives in 2020–2023; leader Helen Houghton) has two websites: the party site conservatives.nz (policy summary, principles, and policy press releases from 2025–26) and a separate 2026 campaign site conservatives.org.nz, linked from the main site, with 14 policy pages (Overview, Health, Economy, Bureaucracy, Environment, Immigration, Policing, Climate, Agriculture, Child Protection, Tax Relief, Right to Life, Natural Resources, Energy). Both are captured; policies are listed below with the campaign page as the main source.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/conservative/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Wix blog posts on conservatives.nz are rendered client-side; their text was recovered from the page's embedded data. The campaign Energy page's layout table extracted poorly (text is present but jumbled). Tax wording differs: the economy page says 'lower tax rate', a 2025 press release says 'flat tax rate'.

## Headline policies

- [Cut personal and company tax, align the company rate with the top personal rate, and lower GST to 12.5%](#cut-personal-and-company-tax-align-the-company-rate-with-the-top-personal-rate-and-lower-gst-to-125-con-01) — Incomes & employment
- [Stop taxing NZ Super (including for over-65s still working) and boarders' income in private homes](#stop-taxing-nz-super-including-for-over-65s-still-working-and-boarders-income-in-private-homes-con-02) — Incomes & employment
- [Tighten immigration toward skilled migrants and cap other net migration by the supply of housing, doctors and school places](#tighten-immigration-toward-skilled-migrants-and-cap-other-net-migration-by-the-supply-of-housing-doctors-and-school-places-con-05) — Migration
- [Leave the Paris Agreement, scrap the ETS and repeal all 'climate'-based taxes, laws and agencies](#leave-the-paris-agreement-scrap-the-ets-and-repeal-all-climate-based-taxes-laws-and-agencies-con-09) — Environment
- [Encourage oil and gas exploration with a Norway-style resource joint venture and sovereign investment fund](#encourage-oil-and-gas-exploration-with-a-norway-style-resource-joint-venture-and-sovereign-investment-fund-con-11) — Economy
- [Recognise an unborn child as a legal person from the third trimester](#recognise-an-unborn-child-as-a-legal-person-from-the-third-trimester-con-17) — Health

## Contents by topic

- [Community & inclusion](#community--inclusion) (1)
- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (1)
- [Economy](#economy) (2)
- [Environment](#environment) (2)
- [Health](#health) (3)
- [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (2)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (5)
- [Migration](#migration) (1)
- [Transport & infrastructure](#transport--infrastructure) (2)

## Community & inclusion

### Employment and services based on merit, 'one law for all', and 'a man is a man, and a woman is a woman' (CON-19)

**Why** (*archive*): The party opposes policies that divide people by race, ancestry, sex or identity.

**How** (*archive*): Listed among its 'policies that work' alongside limiting unskilled immigration and defending free speech and Judeo-Christian traditions.

Full text: [Our Policies](documents/site-policy.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/policy)); [Overview (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-overview.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/overview/))

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Review all trade agreements and pursue a neutral foreign policy with a support- and reconstruction-focused military (CON-18)

**How** (*archive*): Seek a balance between free trade and protectionism ('Trade before War'); avoid being drawn into conflicts that do not threaten NZ territory.

Full text: [Economic and Trade Policy](documents/news-new-policies-announcement.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/new-policies-announcement))

## Economy

### Oppose converting farmland to carbon forestry and oppose the Gene Technology Bill (CON-10)

**How** (*archive*): No incentives for permanent carbon forestry on productive land; keep restrictions on GMO field trials and release; revisit the Planning and Natural Environment Bills to make them workable and protect property rights.

Full text: [Agriculture (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-agriculture.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/agriculture/)); [Policy clarification on rural, environmental, and agricultural issues](documents/news-policy-clarification-on-rural-environmental-and-agricultural-issues.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/policy-clarification-on-rural%2C-environmental%2C-and-agricultural-issues))

### Encourage oil and gas exploration with a Norway-style resource joint venture and sovereign investment fund (CON-11)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says New Zealand has failed to secure a fair share of its resources.

**How** (*archive*): Public-private resource partnerships, royalties shared with local communities, environmental bonds, returns held in a New Zealand Investment Fund.

Full text: [Natural Resources (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-natural-resources.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/natural-resources/))

## Environment

### Leave the Paris Agreement, scrap the ETS and repeal all 'climate'-based taxes, laws and agencies (CON-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says there is no climate emergency and that climate policies raise food and energy costs and hurt the poor most.

**How** (*archive*): Remove fossil-fuel taxes and restrictions, abolish climate units in government, end energy subsidies of any kind, and stop public funding of methane research such as AgriZero.

Full text: [Climate (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-climate.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/climate/)); [Agriculture (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-agriculture.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/agriculture/))

### Create a Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary and overhaul fisheries management with cameras on all commercial vessels (CON-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the sustainable fisheries regime is widely abused.

**How** (*archive*): Promote the Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary Bill and reinstall surveillance cameras on commercial vessels.

Full text: [Environment (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-environment.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/environment/)); [Has New Zealand Failed Its Oceans? Conservative Party Says Yes - Environment Policy update](documents/news-has-new-zealand-failed-its-oceans.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/has-new-zealand-failed-its-oceans))

## Health

### Make cutting hospital waiting times the top health priority, funded from bureaucracy, procurement and productivity savings (CON-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the key issue is whether patients are treated in time, not how much is spent.

**How** (*archive*): Measure waits for elective surgery, specialists, diagnostics, cancer and ED; buy private capacity where it is quicker and competitive; grow the domestic workforce; link any extra funding to measurable results.

Full text: [Health (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-health.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/health/))

### Restrict irreversible gender-related medical procedures for minors and require parental involvement (CON-16)

**How** (*archive*): Independent assessment before significant intervention, evidence-based practice, parental involvement subject to safeguards, and independent review mechanisms.

Full text: [Child Protection (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-child-protection.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/child-protection/))

### Recognise an unborn child as a legal person from the third trimester (CON-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says every human life has inherent dignity.

**How** (*archive*): An Unborn Child (Legal Personhood and Rights) Act with a protected right to life, without criminalising pregnant women, plus a Pregnancy and Family Support Programme (support payment, housing security, support services, adoption options).

Full text: [Right to life (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-right-to-life.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/right-to-life/))

## Incomes & employment

### Cut personal and company tax, align the company rate with the top personal rate, and lower GST to 12.5% (CON-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says lower taxes improve compliance and investment and that New Zealand's rates should be no higher than Australia's.

**How** (*archive*): Also tackle public debt; a 2025 release calls for a 'flat tax rate' for individuals and companies.

Full text: [Economy (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-economy-1.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/economy-1/)); [Economic and Trade Policy](documents/news-new-policies-announcement.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/new-policies-announcement))

### Stop taxing NZ Super (including for over-65s still working) and boarders' income in private homes (CON-02)

**How** (*archive*): Remove NZ Super from taxable income, and exempt genuine home-sharing/boarder income with safeguards against commercial use.

Full text: [Tax Relief (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-superannuation.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/superannuation/))

## Law, justice & government

### Let mayors become full-time council CEOs and give ministers power to appoint and sack senior public servants (CON-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says unelected bureaucrats and advisers usurp the mandate of elected representatives.

**How** (*archive*): Elected representatives at local and national level would get wide powers to dismiss obstructive or incompetent staff; legislate to curtail 'unconstitutional bureaucratic power'.

Full text: [Bureaucracy (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-bureaucracy.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/bureaucracy/)); [Has New Zealand Lost Control of Its Own Government?](documents/news-has-new-zealand-lost-control-of-its-own-government.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/has-new-zealand-lost-control-of-its-own-government))

### Hold a Royal Commission of Inquiry into police under-performance and corruption (CON-06)

**Why** (*archive*): The party cites fabricated drink-drive tests and lost public trust.

**How** (*archive*): Also: refer prima facie criminal allegations against police and all deaths caused by police action to the courts; protect identities of police witnesses in international drug cases; review drone laws.

Full text: [Policing (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-policing.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/policing/)); [Announcement: Police Policy - Commission Of Inquiry Into Under Performance And Corruption](documents/news-police-policy-announcement.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/police-policy-announcement))

### Strengthen the IPCA: double its staff, quadruple its budget, and let it prosecute and name officers (CON-07)

**How** (*archive*): As set out in its 'Sharpening the Teeth of the IPCA' statement.

Full text: [Law & Justice Policy Statement: Sharpening the Teeth of the IPCA](documents/news-sharpening-the-teeth-of-the-ipca.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/sharpening-the-teeth-of-the-ipca))

### Improve access to justice for self-represented litigants (CON-08)

**How** (*archive*): Procedural changes, support services, legal aid reform, tax deductions and cost awards for pro bono work, and wider Family Dispute Resolution.

Full text: [Improving Access to Justice for Self-Represented Litigants](documents/news-press-release-improving-access-to-justice-for-self-represented-litigan.md) ([original](https://www.conservatives.nz/news/press-release---improving-access-to-justice-for-self-represented-litigants))

### Increase penalties for child sexual offending and online exploitation (CON-15)

**How** (*archive*): Longer sentences for serious and repeat offenders, review of sentence reductions, better monitoring after release, more online-exploitation investigation resources and victim support.

Full text: [Child Protection (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-child-protection.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/child-protection/))

## Migration

### Tighten immigration toward skilled migrants and cap other net migration by the supply of housing, doctors and school places (CON-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says population growing faster than 'social goods' makes everyone poorer.

**How** (*archive*): A stable points system; end 'golden' investor visas; NZ licence tests for foreign truck drivers; tougher document checks and audits; report GDP per capita.

Full text: [Immigration (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-immigration.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/immigration/))

## Transport & infrastructure

### Buy a fleet of oil tankers and build new oil refineries for fuel security (CON-12)

**How** (*archive*): Tankers would guarantee supply and floating storage until refineries able to process local and Pacific crude are built; also bring back manufacturing.

Full text: [Natural Resources (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-natural-resources.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/natural-resources/)); [Agriculture (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-agriculture.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/agriculture/))

### Ensure 'cheap, reliable and abundant' energy without relying solely on solar and wind (CON-13)

**How** (*archive*): Renewables have a role but cannot be relied on alone because of variability.

Full text: [Energy (2026 campaign site)](documents/campaign-energy.md) ([original](https://conservatives.org.nz/policies/energy/))

# Free Palestine (Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Free Palestine (Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **6 policies** listed, backed by **3 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://palfree.nz/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 as "Free Palestine" (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

Free Palestine is a single-issue party registered in August 2026 (its website calls it the 'Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party'). Its platform consists of three objectives and six founding principles on its one-page website, the same principles in its June 2026 constitution lodged with the Electoral Commission, and a six-point list in its August 2026 registration press release. Each principle/objective is listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/free-palestine/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The party has no published policies on domestic issues. Wording differs slightly between sources: the website refers to dismantling 'the Zionist structure of the state of Israel', the constitution to 'the apartheid structure'. Media reports of a separate 2026 foreign-affairs policy could not be checked against a party document (web search capacity ran out). The website's membership, enrolment and donation sections are omitted from the captured text.

## Headline policies

- [Support the right of return of Palestinian refugees and the dismantling of Israel's current state structure, rejecting a two-state solution](#support-the-right-of-return-of-palestinian-refugees-and-the-dismantling-of-israels-current-state-structure-rejecting-a-two-state-solution-fpp-01) — Defence & foreign affairs
- [Establish a single secular, democratic, bi-national state in all of historic Palestine with equal citizenship](#establish-a-single-secular-democratic-bi-national-state-in-all-of-historic-palestine-with-equal-citizenship-fpp-02) — Defence & foreign affairs
- [Adopt an independent foreign policy and withdraw from formal military and security alliances with the United States](#adopt-an-independent-foreign-policy-and-withdraw-from-formal-military-and-security-alliances-with-the-united-states-fpp-05) — Defence & foreign affairs

## Contents by topic

- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (6)

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Support the right of return of Palestinian refugees and the dismantling of Israel's current state structure, rejecting a two-state solution (FPP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says a just peace depends on refugees' return and that further partition would bring more injustice.

**How** (*archive*): Founding principle 1 (website) / constitution clause 2.

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

### Establish a single secular, democratic, bi-national state in all of historic Palestine with equal citizenship (FPP-02)

**How** (*archive*): Founding principle 4: one state with full and equal citizenship and ethnic and religious rights protected in a democratic constitution.

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

### Press the New Zealand government to uphold international law and UN resolutions on Palestine and support war-crimes and genocide prosecutions (FPP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says its aim is to change public opinion and put sustained parliamentary pressure on the government.

**How** (*archive*): Accept the primacy of international law and UN resolutions; call Israel to account under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights; have New Zealand support prosecutions and use its independent voice internationally.

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

### Give 'unconditional and complete solidarity' to Palestinian resistance 'in all forms accordant with International Humanitarian Law' (FPP-04)

**How** (*archive*): Founding principle 5 (the press release lists 'unconditional support for all forms of Palestine resistance' without the IHL qualifier).

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

### Adopt an independent foreign policy and withdraw from formal military and security alliances with the United States (FPP-05)

**How** (*archive*): Founding principle 6: leave any formal US security alliances and distance foreign policy from 'Anglo-U.S. economic hegemony and military interventionism'.

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

### Build a mass democratic movement and global solidarity links for Palestinian liberation (FPP-06)

**How** (*archive*): The party's stated objectives: a broad party uniting Palestine supporters from all traditions, and links with others resisting inequality and injustice; it also seeks to persuade other parties to adopt stronger pro-Palestine policies.

Full text: [Palestine Free from the River to the Sea Party — Objectives and Founding Principles](documents/palfree-home-objectives-principles.md) ([original](https://palfree.nz/)); [Free Palestine Party Constitution (June 2026, as lodged with the Electoral Commission)](documents/constitution-june-2026.md) ([original](https://elections.nz/assets/Party-rules/FPP-Constitution-June-2026.pdf)); [The Free Palestine Party: The Newest Political Party In Aotearoa](documents/release-2026-08-newest-political-party.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00073/the-free-palestine-party-the-newest-political-party-in-aotearoa.htm))

# Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand — every 2026 election policy

*Compiled 2026-10-23 for the 7 November 2026 general election. Part of a non-partisan archive; every item links to its source and, wherever it could be retrieved, to the full verbatim text in [`documents/`](documents/).*

## About this page

- **226 policy statements from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz)** (the independent, non-partisan guide), each with its *Why* and *How* summary exactly as policy.nz wrote it, its topics and its citations. These are the core of this page.
- **245 verbatim "Our plan" commitments** from the 38 chapters of the Green Party Manifesto 2026 (launched 26 July 2026), so that every manifesto commitment is listed even where policy.nz did not write it up. These are quoted exactly; they have no separate summary.
- **93 further entries** for party policy documents and 2026 campaign announcements, with a short neutral summary written for this archive (marked `summary_source: "archive"` in [`policies.json`](policies.json)).
- **185 full-text documents** in [`documents/`](documents/): 54 PDFs (manifesto, Māori manifesto, Easy Read manifesto, 40 standing policy papers, 2026 campaign policy papers, Green Budget 2025), 123 greens.org.nz pages and 8 press releases mirrored on Scoop.

**How the text was obtained.** greens.org.nz is behind Cloudflare and refuses automated access (HTTP 403), and the Internet Archive (web.archive.org) could not be reached from the research environment. So:
1. **PDFs** were downloaded directly from the party's file host `assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/…` (and two from `img.scoop.co.nz`) and converted with `pdftotext`. Reading order was checked; the default (non-layout) mode was cleaner for the multi-column brochures, and pages that contain tables are additionally reproduced in `-layout` form so that table rows stay intact. One image-only PDF (the KiwiPower explainer) was transcribed by hand and is marked as such. Local copies are in `raw/party-docs/green/pdf/`.
2. **greens.org.nz web pages** (manifesto chapters, policy summary pages, press releases) were recovered from **Common Crawl** WARC captures (crawls CC-MAIN-2026-30, -34, -39 and -43, i.e. July to 18 October 2026); each document records its capture date.
3. **Press releases not captured by Common Crawl** were taken from the copies the party posted on **scoop.co.nz**.
4. Nothing was paraphrased inside a full-text document. Where a source could not be retrieved the document says so.

**Not retrievable:**
- `greens.org.nz/disability_policy_full`. The Disability Policy PDF it points to now returns HTTP 403, so it appears to have been withdrawn. The disability policy summary page and the manifesto disability chapter are included. See [note](documents/unretrievable-disability-policy-full.md).
- `greens.org.nz/greens_announce_jobs_guarantee_for_young_people` (about 11 Oct 2026). The policy paper it announced is included in full. See [note](documents/unretrievable-greens-announce-jobs-guarantee-for-young-people.md).
- The **fiscal plan released on 23 October 2026** (the day this page was compiled). It is not yet in any crawl or mirror reachable from here. The section below summarises press coverage of it.
- policy.nz also cites two pages from other parties for Green policies (POL54980, POL55038). They are flagged on those entries.

## Headline commitments

policy.nz marks these as the Greens' **key policies**:

- **Create a 2.5 percent tax on assets worth over $10m** (Economy). [POL54655](#pol54655)
- **Implement a tax on wealth received over $1m** (Economy). [POL54729](#pol54729)
- **Increase the corporate tax rate to 33 percent for big corporations only** (Economy). [POL54730](#pol54730)
- **Make the first $10,000 that people earn tax-free** (Incomes and employment). [POL54735](#pol54735)
- **Create a new tax bracket for income earned over $160,000** (Incomes and employment). [POL54737](#pol54737)
- **Establish a government backed clean energy loan scheme** (Environment). [POL54744](#pol54744)
- **Mandate the installation of solar on new or renovated public homes, where appropriate** (Housing). [POL54764](#pol54764)
- **Create a job guarantee programme for jobs focused on ecosystem regeneration** (Incomes and employment). [POL54787](#pol54787)
- **Provide stable funding for creative organisations and events** (Media, culture and recreation). [POL54954](#pol54954)
- **Support the repatriation of taonga overseas back to the Māori community** (Media, culture and recreation). [POL54956](#pol54956)
- **Establish infrastructure across ministries to strengthen our creative and cultural economy** (Media, culture and recreation). [POL54957](#pol54957)
- **Provide $200m towards te reo Māori initiatives** (Te ao Māori). [POL54979](#pol54979)
- **Expand voting rights in New Zealand** (Law, justice and government). [POL54981](#pol54981)
- **Entrench the Māori electoral seats** (Law, justice and government). [POL54982](#pol54982)
- **Strengthen political lobbying rules** (Law, justice and government). [POL54984](#pol54984)
- **Remove barriers to accessing essential services for disabled people** (Health). [POL55004](#pol55004)

The party's campaign is built around three priorities: "affordable living, healthy nature and real democracy". It is to be paid for by taxing "the super-rich and mega-corporations" while cutting income tax "for 96 percent of people" ([manifesto introduction](documents/web-manifesto-2026.md)). The main policy packages released during 2026 were:

- **Tax policy 'A tax system for all of us': wealth tax, capital acquisitions tax, higher tax on big corporates, bank levy, and income tax cuts for 96% of earners**: The 12-page tax plan (announced 21 June 2026). Revenue measures: a 2.5% tax on the net assets of the super-rich above $10 million (family homes exempt); a capital acquisitions tax on gifts and inheritances over $1 million (family farms and homes exempt); a 33% company tax rate for the largest 0.7% of companies while small and medium firms stay at 28%; a 0.06% levy on the liabilities of the four big banks; enforcing a 5% withholding tax on big tech profits sent offshore; and reversing the coalition's landlord interest-deductibility and bright-line changes. Income tax: a $10,000 tax-free threshold, new stepped brackets and a 45% rate above $160,000. The party's own Parliamentary-Library-based modelling puts the net gain at about $5.1-5.7 billion a year (2027/28-2030/31). [full text](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md)
- **'Drink Swim Fish' freshwater and oceans policy**: A 4-page water policy (announced 6 July 2026) aimed at safe drinking water, swimmable rivers and healthier oceans: science-based national freshwater limits including lower nitrate limits, stronger wastewater-discharge rules, phasing out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser, phasing out bottom trawling and other destructive fishing, protecting at least 30% of oceans, and reviewing the fisheries quota system. [full text](documents/drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.md)
- **'Power for all of us' energy policy: Kiwipower, Warmer Kiwi Homes expansion, community energy and zero-interest solar loans**: The 12-page energy policy (announced 20 July 2026). It proposes 'Kiwipower', a publicly owned company to contract and build electricity firming; an expanded Warmer Kiwi Homes insulation/heating programme; $200m for community-owned energy; a government-backed Clean Energy Loans Scheme (modelled as zero-interest, tied to the property) for rooftop solar and other home energy upgrades; and other electricity-market changes. It includes four-year cost tables and says spending would be funded by the proposed super-rich tax. [full text](documents/power-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md)
- **Te Waonui a Tāne: an ongoing, protected funding source for marae**: An 11-page policy (announced 9 August 2026) to recognise and resource marae as social and cultural infrastructure. It proposes a Rangatiratanga Trust with a $2.44 billion Crown funding input, including a $2 billion intergenerational fund (Te Tōtara Haemata) and annual restoration funding for marae, governed with regional marae representation. [full text](documents/te-waonui-a-tane-policy-2026.md)
- **'Affordable food for all of us': KiwiMart public supermarket chain, stronger grocery regulation and a Fair Food Fund**: A 15-page food-system policy (announced 6 September 2026). It proposes a publicly owned supermarket chain 'KiwiMart' (estimated acquisition and capitalisation cost about $2.8bn, citing an estimate of $1.3bn to buy 120 stores and two distribution centres), more Commerce Commission funding and higher penalties for grocery-sector breaches, a $150m Fair Food Fund for community food security, and more funding for regional food providers. [full text](documents/affordable-food-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md)
- **'Safe, sovereign AI': regulate artificial intelligence for the public good**: An 8-page AI plan (announced 12 October 2026). It proposes rules so that AI does not replace human or democratic decision-making (no fully automated decisions with substantive effects in public services), protects data sovereignty, privacy and creators' work, operates within environmental limits (including controls on data centres), shares benefits rather than concentrating them, and is transparent and accountable. [full text](documents/ai-policy-2026-safe-sovereign-ai.md)
- **Youth Jobs Guarantee: a job or training pathway for every 16-24-year-old out of work for six months**: A 7-page jobs policy (published October 2026) guaranteeing every 16-to-24-year-old who has been out of work for six months a pathway into a locally based job or training, delivered with councils and building on the Mayors Taskforce for Jobs. The document's indicative costings rise from $604m in the first year to $1,631m in the fourth. [full text](documents/youth-jobs-guarantee-policy-2026.md)
- **Paid placements for trainee nurses, teachers and social workers; abolish the training wage for apprentices**: A 4-page workforce policy (16-17 October 2026): a universal weekly payment for students during compulsory practical placements (nursing, teaching, social work and similar), relocation support, abolition of the training-wage exemption so apprentices get at least the minimum wage, a grant for apprentices' tools, and more pastoral support. Indicative costs are about $75-80m and $117m a year for the two parts. [full text](documents/paid-placements-apprenticeships-policy-2026.md)
- **Connect: Aotearoa transport plan**: 4 Oct 2026: transport plan with free public transport for children, students, Community Service Card holders and Total Mobility users, a $2 fare cap for everyone else, bus lanes in the three main cities and mass rapid transit. [full text](documents/web-green-party-launches-the-transport-plan-to-combat-fossil-fuel-crisis.md), [policy page](documents/web-connect-aotearoa.md)

**Fiscal plan (23 October 2026).** The party released its overall fiscal plan at Parliament on 23 October 2026. The document itself could not be retrieved here. According to [RNZ's report](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/2097318/green-party-releases-fiscal-plan-promises-to-increase-health-spending-by-3-billion-each-year) (Russell Palmer, 23 Oct 2026), the plan:
- adds $3 billion to health funding in each of the next four Budgets, about $30 billion over the period;
- relies on "nearly $29 billion in extra revenue over four years" from the wealth tax, the tax on large gifts and inheritances, higher company tax for big businesses, a bank levy and landlord tax changes, alongside income tax cuts for most workers;
- raises future operating allowances to $4.5b–$4.7b a year, compared with about $2.4b under the coalition's plans;
- returns to surplus in 2029/30, a year later than Treasury forecasts, and leaves debt $26.6 billion higher than Treasury expects by 2030/31;
- commits future Budget funding to buying overseas carbon credits. Treasury estimated that bill could reach $5 billion; the Greens say more domestic cuts would reduce it.
Infometrics reviewed the plan's direct fiscal effects. Swarbrick said every election policy had been costed, and that the party still wants a Parliamentary Budget Office. National (Simeon Brown) and ACT (David Seymour) criticised the plan; their reactions are in the same RNZ report. Other outlets' coverage gave a debt figure of 44% of GDP by 2030/31 against Treasury's 39.5%. That figure has not been verified against the party document.

**Costings in individual policy papers.** Most 2026 policy papers end with four-year cost tables (2027/28–2030/31). These include [Power for all of us](documents/power-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md), [KiwiPower](documents/kiwipower-explainer-2026.md), [Te Waonui a Tāne](documents/te-waonui-a-tane-policy-2026.md), [Affordable food](documents/affordable-food-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.md), [Youth Jobs Guarantee](documents/youth-jobs-guarantee-policy-2026.md) and [Paid placements & apprenticeships](documents/paid-placements-apprenticeships-policy-2026.md). Release-level costings include pay equity for care workers (about $1.1bn a year), cancelling public-service cuts ($3.17bn over four years) and te reo Māori ($200m). The party's 2025 alternative budget, [Green Budget 2025](documents/green-budget-2025.md), includes a full fiscal summary.

## Economy

### Policies (policy.nz)

<a id="pol54655"></a>
**Create a 2.5 percent tax on assets worth over $10m** ⭐ key policy  
`POL54655` · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, tax-and-income-support, key-policies-economy, government-revenue-and-finance

- **Why:** This party says that the richest 311 households in NZ pay an effective tax rate of 9 percent, half that of most working people. This is because much of this wealth sits in asset portfolios, rather than being taxed as income. The wealthy need to contribute to solving shared problems with the rest of New Zealand. With the 150 richest people in NZ holding as much as 917,000 households, it is important to ensure the wealthy contribute through taxes.
- **How:** This party would implement a 2.5 percent annual tax on the net assets of people holding over $10m in wealth. This would affect 0.3 percent of New Zealanders.
- **Full text:** ['A tax system for all of us' (PDF), undated](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/71965/attachments/original/1782084525/GreensTaxPolicy2026.pdf?1782084525)); ['Income', undated (accessed 13 August 2026)](documents/web-manifesto-2026-income.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_income))

<a id="pol54729"></a>
**Implement a tax on wealth received over $1m** ⭐ key policy  
`POL54729` · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, tax-and-income-support, key-policies-economy, government-revenue-and-finance

- **Why:** This party says that more than $1.6 trillion in wealth is passed on intergenerationally. The party believes that being rich shouldn't be determined by who your parents are.
- **How:** This party would introduce a Capital Acquisitions Tax on assets and gifts received worth more than $1m. Family farms and family homes would be exempt.
- **Full text:** ['A tax system for all of us' (PDF), undated](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/71965/attachments/original/1782084525/GreensTaxPolicy2026.pdf?1782084525)); ['Policy Announcement - A tax system for all of us', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-tax-system-for-all.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/tax_system_for_all))

<a id="pol54730"></a>
**Increase the corporate tax rate to 33 percent for big corporations only** ⭐ key policy  
`POL54730` · topics: economy, incomes-and-employment, business-support, government-revenue-and-finance, key-policies-economy, tax-and-income-support

- **Why:** This party says that large corporations in NZ are profiting from the public without contributing back towards society. It says that cuts to the corporate tax rate have not increased wellbeing, growth or investment for most New Zealanders; rather, corporations see more profits.
- **How:** This party would return the corporate tax rate to 33 percent for the 0.7 percent biggest corporations, such as the supermarket duopoly, energy companies, and banks. It would keep the corporate tax rate at  28 percent for small and medium enterprises. It would also introduce a Bank Levy of 0.06 percent on the liabilities of the four main banks. It would also enforce the 5 percent tax rate on service and license fees for large tech companies.
- **Full text:** ['A tax system for all of us' (PDF), undated](documents/tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-us.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/71965/attachments/original/1782084525/GreensTaxPolicy2026.pdf?1782084525)); ['Policy Announcement - A tax system for all of us', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-tax-system-for-all.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/tax_system_for_all))

<a id="pol54742"></a>
**Phase out certain fishing practices**  
`POL54742` · topics: economy, environment, fisheries, oceans, conservation

- **Why:** This party says that bottom trawling, set netting, dredging and seamounts are destructive fishing practices, destroying native ecosystems and catching endangered species such as the Māui and Hector's dolphins. Banning these fishing practices would protect NZ's ocean ecosystems for generations to come.
- **How:** This party would phase out bottom trawling, set netting and dredging, starting with an immediate ban on seamounts. The focus on banning these fishing practices would begin in ecologically sensitive areas such as Tīkapa Moana/Hauraki Gulf and the habitats of Māui and Hector's dolphins.
- **Full text:** ['Oceans and Fisheries', undated (accessed 13 August 2026)](documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-fisheries.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_oceans_and_fisheries)); ['Drink Swim Fish Fixing the rules for fresh water and oceans' (PDF), undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/74309/attachments/original/1783476578/DSF_Policy_2026.pdf?1783476578)); ['Policy Announcement - Drink, Swim, Fish — Fixing the rules for water', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-drink-swim-fish.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/drink_swim_fish))

<a id="pol54743"></a>
**Review the quota system for fisheries**  
`POL54743` · topics: economy, environment, fisheries, oceans

- **Why:** This party says that the current fisheries rules allow for overfishing, depleting NZ's oceans. It wants to replenish our fish stocks with an improved management system which is founded on ecosystem protection.
- **How:** This party would review the Quota Management System and move towards ecosystem-based fisheries management that prioritises abundance and long-term sustainability.
- **Full text:** ['Oceans and Fisheries', undated (accessed 13 August 2026)](documents/web-manifesto-2026-oceans-and-fisheries.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/manifesto_2026_oceans_and_fisheries)); ['Drink Swim Fish Fixing the rules for fresh water and oceans' (PDF), undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.md) ([original](https://assets.nationbuilder.com/beachheroes/pages/74309/attachments/original/1783476578/DSF_Policy_2026.pdf?1783476578)); ['Policy Announcement - Drink, Swim, Fish — Fixing the rules for water', undated (accessed 24 August 2026)](documents/web-drink-swim-fish.md) ([original](https://www.greens.org.nz/drink_swim_fish))

<a id="pol54902"></a>
**Implement Waitangi Tribunal recommendations to ensure governance of the agricultural sector upholds Te Tiriti o Waitangi.**  
`POL54902` · topics: economy, te-ao-maori, agriculture, te-reo-maori-and-culture, te-tiriti-o-waitangi-and-governance

- **Why:** This party says that governance of the agricultural sector should recognise the expertise and rights of Māori and have self-governance over mahinga kai (food production). The agriculture sector and regional councils should work in partnership with Māori, in line with Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
