# Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party (ALCP) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party (ALCP)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **11 policies** listed, backed by **1 full-text source document**.

- Party website: <https://www.alcp.org.nz/>
- Registration: 30 May 1996 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The ALCP's policy page ("Full Spectrum Policy") is a single document, credited as developed in 2005 by Irinka Britnell, Paula Lambert and Kevin O'Connell, with a 'Policy Minimum Programme', eleven numbered portfolio sections and a 2020 addendum of ideas 'under discussion' prepared for the cannabis referendum bill. The party presents this page as its current policy; each distinct commitment is listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/legalise-cannabis/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The policy text is largely from 2005 with a 2020 addendum; no 2026-specific manifesto, costings or press releases were captured (the site's News page was not mined, and web search capacity ran out during this research). The 2020 items are described by the party as 'under discussion and in progress'.

## Headline policies

- [Make possession, cultivation and use of cannabis free from prosecution](#make-possession-cultivation-and-use-of-cannabis-free-from-prosecution-alcp-01) — Law, justice & government
- [Create regulated R18 cannabis commerce like alcohol and tobacco, but with no promotion](#create-regulated-r18-cannabis-commerce-like-alcohol-and-tobacco-but-with-no-promotion-alcp-02) — Health
- [Expunge all cannabis convictions and apologise for prohibition](#expunge-all-cannabis-convictions-and-apologise-for-prohibition-alcp-05) — Law, justice & government

## Contents by topic

- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (1)
- [Economy](#economy) (2)
- [Health](#health) (3)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (4)
- [Migration](#migration) (1)

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Reallocate drug-war resources to border security and civil defence (ALCP-10)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the international war on drugs aids organised crime and terrorism.

**How** (*archive*): Resources freed by ending the cannabis 'drug war' would strengthen border security and civil defence.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

## Economy

### Enable full-scale hemp production, prioritising local low-cost biofuel, fibre and hurd (ALCP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says hemp would create jobs (especially in depressed regions), cut emissions and pollution, save forests and improve soils.

**How** (*archive*): Allow full-scale cannabis-hemp farming and use, with priority for localised biofuel production and fibre and hurd for building materials, paper, plastics and textiles; hemp seed as food.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

### Allow at least five cannabis plants per household and affordable micro-licences for small growers (ALCP-11)

**Why** (*archive*): Part of the party's 2020 'cottage industry' ideas, which it says are still under discussion.

**How** (*archive*): A 'bare minimum' five-plant home-grow allowance, affordable micro-licences for existing growers, Kiwi seed strains, safe edibles, quality-controlled retail products and protection against racially loaded enforcement; an age limit more consistent with alcohol and tobacco.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

## Health

### Create regulated R18 cannabis commerce like alcohol and tobacco, but with no promotion (ALCP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The ALCP says cannabis prohibition is unworkable and discriminatory, wastes public money and fuels the black market.

**How** (*archive*): Legal adult-only sales with no advertising or promotional aspects, with details fine-tuned by a policy council.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

### Provide for medicinal cannabis, including home-grown medicine and prescribed preparations (ALCP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says legal access would promote safer modes of use such as vaporisation and mouth sprays.

**How** (*archive*): Establish therapeutic applications of cannabis, allowing both home-grown medicinal cannabis and prescribed preparations.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

### Set up a tobacco, alcohol and cannabis authority (Drugs Policy Council) to regulate recreational substances (ALCP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says credible, harm-reduction drug education is impossible under current 'double standards'.

**How** (*archive*): A single regulator to develop the regulatory framework for recreational substances, with 'adults only' enforcement and honest drug education in schools funded from prohibition savings.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

## Law, justice & government

### Make possession, cultivation and use of cannabis free from prosecution (ALCP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The ALCP says cannabis prohibition is unworkable and discriminatory, wastes public money and fuels the black market.

**How** (*archive*): Part of the party's 'Policy Minimum Programme': no prosecution for possessing, growing or using cannabis and cannabis/hemp products.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

### Expunge all cannabis convictions and apologise for prohibition (ALCP-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says up to 20,000 people a year are convicted of cannabis offences and that Māori are four to five times more likely to be convicted.

**How** (*archive*): Wipe all cannabis convictions; the 2020 addendum adds that apologies must be made for the injustices of prohibition.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

### Hold a prohibition 'truth and reconciliation' commission (ALCP-06)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says Parliament has a duty to challenge injustice and break down prejudice.

**How** (*archive*): A full commission on prohibition 'in the interests of accountability'.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

### Redirect prohibition enforcement money to health, education, community and serious crime (ALCP-08)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says police would be freed up for 'real crime' and public trust in the law would improve.

**How** (*archive*): Shift funds currently spent enforcing cannabis laws into health, education, community and employment, and more police and court resources for serious crime.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

## Migration

### Stop overseas cannabis offences being a barrier to immigrating to New Zealand (ALCP-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says it has no other immigration position beyond inclusiveness and tolerance.

**How** (*archive*): Cannabis offences in other jurisdictions should not bar migrants.

Full text: [Full Spectrum Policy (ALCP policy page)](documents/full-spectrum-policy.md) ([original](https://www.alcp.org.nz/policy))

## Source documents

# National Party — 2026 election policies

Every 2026 general-election policy of the New Zealand National Party (Te Rōpū Nāhinara) that this archive could find, with a short summary of each and links to the **full verbatim text** of National's own policy documents, web pages and press releases.

- **159 policies**: 126 from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz) (the Why/How summaries are policy.nz's neutral summaries) plus 33 further commitments found in National's own documents that policy.nz does not list separately (summaries written by this archive, marked `NAT-ARC-xx`).
- **136 source documents** in [`documents/`](documents/): 36 PDF policy documents, 40 policy pages from national.org.nz, 57 National Party press releases/speeches, and 3 third-party pages cited by policy.nz (Beehive, RNZ).
- Retrieved **2026-10-23** directly from national.org.nz / assets.national.org.nz (policy hub: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies>), beehive.govt.nz and rnz.co.nz. Original PDFs and HTML are kept in `raw/party-docs/national/`. Scripts: `tools/policies_national_*.py`.
- Policy statements, Why/How summaries and topics for `POL…` entries come from policy.nz (`raw/policy.nz/parties/national-party.json`). Costings are shown only where National or policy.nz states one.
- National is the senior party in the current (2023–2026) coalition Government, so some documents mix new election promises with descriptions of what the Government has already done. Entries here are the forward-looking commitments.

## Contents

- [Key commitments / headline policies](#key-commitments--headline-policies)
- [Costings & fiscal plan](#costings--fiscal-plan)
- Policies by topic:
  - [Economy](#economy) (46)
  - [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (12)
  - [Health](#health) (14)
  - [Education](#education) (19)

  - [Environment](#environment) (14)

- [All source documents](#all-source-documents)

## Key commitments / headline policies

National's campaign slogan is “Fixing the Basics. Building the Future.” Its central promises, as set out on its policy hub, “Our Plan” page and campaign launch, are:

- No new taxes in the next term (including no capital gains tax), and keep Investment Boost — [POL54733](#introduce-no-new-taxes-in-the-next-term-of-government), [NAT-ARC-20](#keep-investment-boost)
- Return to surplus in 2028/29, keep net core Crown debt below 40% of GDP, spending towards 30% of GDP (Budget Responsibility Rules) — [POL54725](#create-a-government-surplus-by-202829), [POL54726](#keep-government-debt-below-40-percent-of-gdp), [POL54727](#keep-crown-expenditure-close-to-30-per-cent-of-gdp)
- Make KiwiSaver compulsory from 1 July 2028 (combined contributions rising to 12% by 2032), $1,500 “Baby Boost” and auto-enrolment at birth, KiwiSaver top-up during paid parental leave, employer contributions for over-65s — [POL54734](#enrol-new-zealand-citizens-in-kiwisaver-at-birth)
- Extend paid parental leave from 26 to 30 weeks by 2029 — [POL54715](#increase-paid-parental-leave-to-30-weeks-by-2029)
- Widen 5% deposit First Home Loans (income cap raised to $300,000) — [POL54918](#raise-the-income-threshold-for-people-who-can-pay-a-lower-deposit-for-their-first-home)
- Cut the student loan repayment rate from 12% to 10% and get tougher on overseas defaulters — [POL54813](#reduce-the-student-loan-repayment-rate-to-10-percent), [POL54814](#fund-further-enforcement-and-create-harsher-penalties-for-overseas-based-student-loan-holders)
- A further $604m for Pharmac, bowel screening from age 50, breast screening to 74, free cervical screening 25–69 — [POL55205](#increase-funding-for-pharmacs-medicines-budget), [POL55208](#lower-the-free-bowel-screening-age-to-50-by-2029), [POL55209](#extend-free-breast-screening-extension-to-age-74-by-2029), [POL55211](#deliver-free-cervical-screening-for-all-women-aged-25-to-69)
- Pursue structural separation of Foodstuffs into two competing nationwide grocery groups (subject to Commerce Commission assessment) — [POL55014](#separate-the-foodstuffs-business-into-two-nationwide-cooperatives)
- Cap council rate rises (2–4%) — [POL54817](#instruct-councils-to-keep-annual-rate-increases-between-2-and-4-percent)
- Firmer welfare: work support for 30,000 jobseekers, lower rate after two years, drug testing, five-year residency rule — [POL55226](#provide-targeted-work-support-to-30000-jobseekers), [POL55227](#reduce-benefit-payments-for-people-receiving-support-for-more-than-2-years), [POL55228](#introduce-drug-testing-for-people-receiving-benefits), [POL55230](#change-entitlements-for-benefits-for-new-nz-residents-to-5-years)
- Replace NCEA; keep students at school until end of Year 11; no screens in ECE; ban under-16s from social media — [POL55174](#replace-ncea-with-a-different-grading-system), [POL55259](#require-students-to-finish-year-11-before-leaving-school), [POL55050](#limit-the-use-of-screens-in-school-for-primary-aged-and-younger-children), [POL54815](#ban-under-16-year-olds-from-social-media)
- Big transport builds: Belfast–Pegasus/Woodend Bypass ($800m), Mill Road Stage One ($1.75b), next Roads of National Significance — [POL55201](#fund-800-million-christchurch-northern-motorway-extension), [NAT-ARC-01](#fund-construction-of-mill-road-stage-one-manukau-to-alfriston-in-south-auckland), [POL55177](#complete-construction-on-the-next-set-of-roads-of-national-significance)

## Costings & fiscal plan

National published a **Fiscal Plan** ([full text](documents/pdf-nationals-fiscal-plan.md); [web page](documents/policy-nationals-fiscal-plan.md)) and **Budget Responsibility Rules** ([full text](documents/pdf-nationals-budget-responsibility-rules.md)). In summary (all figures are National's own):

- Operating allowances of $2.4 billion per Budget; capital allowances of $3.5 billion for Budgets 2027 and 2028 and $5 billion thereafter.
- Election commitments total $16,450.7 million operating over 2026/27–2030/31, leaving $7,549.3 million of operating allowance unallocated; National says health makes up 88 per cent of its spending commitments.
- Savings counted: reducing the foreign aid budget (−$431.2m) and stronger welfare expectations/case management (−$583.0m).
- Capital commitments of $1,093.5 million (Budget 2027) and $1,750 million (Budget 2028, Mill Road Stage One).
- A re-elected National Government would not impose new taxes, return to surplus in 2028/29 and keep debt below 40 per cent of GDP; National says it would consider tax relief only once the books are back in surplus.

## Economy

#### Invest $50m in roads and rail lines to create a transport hub in Rolleston

`POL54693` · topics: economy, transport-and-infrastructure, regional-development, rail-transport, cars-and-roads, economic-development-and-industry, infrastructure-funding-and-planning, agriculture · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that Rolleston is a well-placed hub for moving goods around, as it is on State Highway 1, the main southern train line, and connected by road and rail to the West Coast. Because many agricultural goods are moved through this area, making it easier to move goods between trains and trucks will increase efficiency and economic opportunity for producers in this area.
- **How:** This party would invest $50m in a road and rail "intermodal hub" in Rolleston. This funding would be dependent on the result of a business case, where private freight companies and customers would also invest in the hub. It would only go ahead with a mix of public and private funding. This party estimates that this policy would cost $50m.
- **Costing:** This party estimates that this policy would cost $50m.
- **Full text:** [National's South Island Plan](documents/pdf-nationals-south-island-plan.md) (PDF) · [National backs South Island growth](documents/news-260814-national-backs-south-island-growth.md) (press release) · [National backs South Island growth](documents/policy-hunters-and-anglers.md) (policy page)

#### Change the policy settings for farmers leasing high country land from the Crown

`POL54696` · topics: economy, environment, agriculture, conservation · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that the Crown owns 1.2 million hectares of land through the South Island, which is leased to farmers for pastoral grazing. Much of this land is at higher elevations. Farmers need certainty about which kinds of activities they can do on this land without requiring consent. Giving farmers other income sources on this land, like beekeeping or horticulture, would provide farmers with the confidence to invest and diversify.
- **How:** This party would pass a law implementing changed policy settings for the kinds of activity to be carried out on Crown pastoral land, and for when farmers need approval or consent for activities.
- **Full text:** [National's South Island Plan](documents/pdf-nationals-south-island-plan.md) (PDF) · [National backs South Island growth](documents/news-260814-national-backs-south-island-growth.md) (press release) · [Unlocking economic potential for high country farms](documents/beehive-unlocking-economic-potential-high-country-farms.md) (external) · [National backs South Island growth](documents/policy-hunters-and-anglers.md) (policy page)

#### Charge international visitors to access locations like Milford Sound, Aoraki, Cathedral Cove and the Tongariro Crossing

`POL54697` · topics: economy, environment, tourism, conservation · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that international tourists are key parts of the economy, especially those who want to see natural attractions. These are managed by the Department of Conservation, and while New Zealanders could continue accessing them for free, tourists should pay some costs towards the upkeep. This money would be invested into tourist infrastructure at these locations.
- **How:** This party would charge international visitors for access to a handful of key NZ attractions from 2027. This money would be largely reinvested in tourist infrastructure and conservation efforts in these areas. This is expected to raise $60 million per year.
- **Full text:** [National backs South Island growth](documents/news-260814-national-backs-south-island-growth.md) (press release) · [National's South Island Plan](documents/pdf-nationals-south-island-plan.md) (PDF) · [Landmark Conservation Reform Bill will boost economy and protect nature](documents/news-20260507-hontamapotaka.md) (press release) · [National backs South Island growth](documents/policy-hunters-and-anglers.md) (policy page)

#### Create timeframes and regional performance metrics for businesses on conservation land

`POL54699` · topics: economy, environment, tourism, conservation, economic-development-and-industry, business-support · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that tourism on conservation land is important to the New Zealand economy. `POL54700` · topics: economy, environment, regional-development, climate-adaptation, agriculture, oil-gas-and-mining · summary: policy.nz

#### Approve data centres only when they are accompanied by more power production

`POL54702` · topics: economy, transport-and-infrastructure, incomes-and-employment, economic-development-and-industry, internet-and-digital-technologies, energy, prices, artificial-intelligence-ai · summary: policy.nz

#### Allow Kiwisaver to be used by farm workers buying homes or farms

`POL54836` · topics: economy, incomes-and-employment, housing, agriculture, superannuation-and-savings, housing-affordability, key-policies-housing · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that that the Kiwisaver policy was designed with urban housing in mind. Farm workers may be living in provided housing, and not able to access Kiwisaver for a house, as they are not living in the home. This means that people working on farms have to wait longer to buy property. Similarly, Kiwisaver withdrawals cannot be used for purchasing a farm through a company. This change will allow people to buy their first farms with less debt.

#### Distribute money from the international visitor levy directly to councils

`POL54897` · topics: economy, law-justice-and-government, tourism, local-government, government-revenue-and-finance, regional-development · summary: policy.nz

Distributing the international visitor levy money not committed to the Department of Conservation and a tourism growth fund to councils is an alternative to a bed tax, which would disproportionately affect domestic tourists in New Zealand. #### Create standard rules for on-site small solar and hydro energy projects

`POL54924` · topics: economy, transport-and-infrastructure, environment, agriculture, energy, emissions-reduction, urban-planning-and-resource-management, regional-development · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that small battery, solar and hydro projects have confusing regulations, making it hard for users like farmers to use natural resources on their own land. From the perspective of energy resilience and affordability, there should be standard and predictable rules so that it is easier for more people to build energy projects on their property. #### Increase paid parental leave to 30 weeks by 2029

`POL54715` · topics: incomes-and-employment, community-and-inclusion, benefits, tax-and-income-support, young-people, key-policies-community-and-inclusion · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that parents need more flexibility for taking leave, including taking paid leave at the same time as their partner, so they can receive more support if needed. Current arrangements create financial penalties for people who take time off work to care for their children. Both parents should have the opportunity to access parental leave if they choose.
- **How:** This party would increase parental leave to 27 weeks in the 2027 budget, with further increases in 2028 and 2029. This leave could be split between parents or shared in overlapping periods. After returning to work, pay for annual leave would be calculated based on yearly salaries, rather than average pay for parents who have earned less due to taking parental leave. This party would also continue contributing to a parent's Kiwisaver while they take paid parental leave. Eventually, this party would aim to increase paid parental leave to 40 weeks.

#### Separate the Foodstuffs business into two nationwide cooperatives

`POL55014` · topics: incomes-and-employment, economy, prices, economic-development-and-industry, key-policies-economy · summary: policy.nz

#### Raise the income threshold for people who can pay a lower deposit for their first home

`POL54918` · topics: housing, incomes-and-employment, housing-affordability, superannuation-and-savings, key-policies-housing · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that a home is an essential way for New Zealanders to build wealth. The First Home Loan scheme has operated since 2003, allowing people to purchase their first homes with a 5% deposit, instead of a standard 20% deposit. However, some people who are struggling to afford the deposit on their first home fall above the income cap of $95,000 for a person buying alone and $150,000 for two people buying together (both with no dependents). Raising the eligibility criteria will mean more people can buy homes with low deposits. Raising and simplifying the eligibility will allow more people to buy houses.

These lower deposits would only apply to people purchasing their first property. The loans would be approved by banks, as already happens, meaning no-one would be issued with a loan they cannot afford. The fiscal impact of this policy is expected to be between $4m-$6m.

#### Double the number of places on the voluntary vet bonding scheme

`POL55321` · topics: community-and-inclusion, economy, education, animal-welfare, agriculture, tertiary-fees-and-student-support · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that many of NZ's young vet's are moving to other countries, which is a problem for the agriculture industry. The number of places in Massey University's vet training programme is increasing by 15 students from 2027, and this party also wants to increase the number of students who can sign up for the voluntary bonding scheme, which provides a financial incentive to new vets who commit to working in rural areas for a time after graduating.
- **How:** This party would double the vet bonding scheme to 70 places each year from the 2027 funding round. The scheme would also be open to NZ citizens and permanent residents who have trained in accredited Australian vet schools and are qualified to work in NZ. There would be reporting on results from the scheme each year, an a full review after three years. This party estimates that this would cost $2m each year once fully implemented, with the money coming from MPI baseline funding.

## Media, culture & recreation

#### Rule out a licence for recreational sea fishing

`POL55263` · topics: media-culture-and-recreation, economy, sports-and-recreation, fisheries, tourism · summary: policy.nz

- **Why:** This party says that at least 600,000 New Zealanders go fishing occasionally, and recreational fish provides food and enjoyment, as well as supporting the business of charter boat tourism for fishing access. Fish stocks need to be maintained for recreational users, but fishing for food is a right and should not require a licence. This party says that honorary Fisheries Officers, who do enforcement work on a voluntary basis, could be doing more of the work of fisheries enforcement.
- **How:** This party would ensure that no licence is required for sea fishing. It would ban the commercial sale of marlin, so hunting this fish can continue to be a sport. Enforcement and fines for people who do not obey catch limits would be increased, and part of this enforcement would be carried out by increasing the number of Honorary Fisheries Officers to 200 around the country. There would be some instant fines for people who catch more than the limit of fish.

# New Zealand First — 2026 election policies

Every 2026 policy of New Zealand First that this archive could find, with a short neutral summary (**Why** — the reason the party gives; **How** — what it would do) and links to the **full verbatim text** of the party's own documents in [`documents/`](documents/). Election day: 7 November 2026. Compiled 23 October 2026.

## At a glance

- **79 policies** listed: 39 from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz) (all of its 39 NZ First statements, with its Why/How summaries) + 40 more found in the party's own releases, speeches and policy PDFs (marked *archive*; summaries written for this archive).
- **104 full-text documents** archived (47 party web pages via Common Crawl, 53 press releases/speeches via Scoop, 4 PDFs) + 7 placeholder file(s) for cited pages that could not be retrieved.
- 79 policies have at least one retrieved party text; 0 rely only on a page that could not be retrieved.

## Method & sources

1. Started from policy.nz's NZ First data (`raw/policy.nz/parties/nz-first.json`): statement, Why/How, citations.
2. nzfirst.nz blocks automated access (Cloudflare 403, also with a headless browser) and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment. The party's own web pages were therefore recovered from **Common Crawl**: its 2026 crawl indexes (CC-MAIN-2026-12 … -43) were searched for every nzfirst.nz URL and the latest HTTP-200 capture of each page was read from the WARC archive on data.commoncrawl.org (`tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_index.py`, `tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_fetch.py`). Each such document (`documents/site-*.md`) records the capture date and WARC record; captures date from 2026-07-19 to 2026-10-14, so later edits are not reflected.
3. In addition, every New Zealand First press release and speech from late 2025 to 23 Oct 2026 was collected from Scoop's organisation page (https://info.scoop.co.nz/New_Zealand_First_Party); Scoop republishes party releases as issued, so their text is the party's own. Policy PDFs the party attached to releases (img.scoop.co.nz) or linked from its site (Google Drive) were downloaded and text-extracted.
4. Each policy links (a) the page policy.nz cited (now mostly a Common Crawl capture) and (b) other party texts on the same policy. Where a cited page could not be recovered at all, a `documents/not-retrieved-*.md` file records the URL and the reason; it contains no paraphrase.
5. Policies found in party texts but missing from policy.nz were added with neutral summaries (`summary_source: archive`). Calls on the current government and positions (e.g. opposing a bill) are included where the party presents them as what it stands for, and are labelled as such.

### Retrieval gaps (read this)

- **7 nzfirst.nz pages cited by policy.nz were not retrieved** (403 / archive unreachable). Where a party release covers the same policy it is linked, but the website page may contain details the release does not.
  - ['NZFirst to Ban Public Sales of Fireworks', 9 October 2026 (accessed 09 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-nzfirst-to-ban-public-sales-of-fireworks.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/nzfirst_to_ban_public_sales_of_fireworks> (policies: POL55234)
  - ['NZ First to Increase Working for Families, Minimum Wage', 10 October 2026 (accessed 12 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-nz-first-to-increase-working-for-families-minimum-wage.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/nz_first_to_increase_working_for_families_minimum_wage> (policies: POL55257, POL55258)
  - ['NZFirst to Scrap Accredited Working Visa Model', 11 October 2026 (accessed 12 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-nzfirst-to-scrap-accredited-working-visa-model.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/nzfirst_to_scrap_accredited_working_visa_model> (policies: POL55262)
  - ['NZ First to increase funding and support to NZ Coastguard', 15 October 2026 (accessed 15 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-increase-funding-and-support-to-nz-coastguard.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/increase_funding_and_support_to_nz_coastguard> (policies: POL55304)
  - ['NZFirst Policy Announcement: Changes to Fast-Track Residential Approvals', 14 October 2026 (accessed 14 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-nzfirst-policy-announcement-changes-to-fast-track-residential.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/nzfirst_policy_announcement_changes_to_fast_track_residential_approvals> (policies: POL55305)
  - ['NZ First Will Immediately Reverse This Week’s Decision by the Minister of Consumer Affairs', 17 October 2026 (accessed 17 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-nz-first-will-immediately-reverse-this-week-s-decision-by-the.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/nz_first_will_immediately_reverse_this_week_s_decision_by_the_minister_of_consumer_affairs> (policies: POL55308)
  - ['NZ First Announces Overhaul to Regulate Combat Sports', 15 October 2026 (accessed 17 October 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-nzfirst-nz-first-announces-overhaul-to-regulate-combat-sports.md) — <https://www.nzfirst.nz/nz_first_announces_overhaul_to_regulate_combat_sports> (policies: POL55309)
- nzfirst.nz's policy index (captured 11 Oct 2026) lists 20 policy pages, all recovered from Common Crawl. Seven pages policy.nz cites (October 2026 announcements) had no capture; the identical-titled Scoop releases are linked instead.
- The site's 'Our Members' Bills' list is paginated; only its first page and the individual bill pages that were captured are archived. Bills dated 2025 are included because the party still lists them as its members' bills; they are grouped separately.
- parliament.nz / legislation.govt.nz could not be fetched (bot-protection). Bill drafts the party itself published are archived as PDFs: anti-scam, accessibility, fireworks, container return.
- policy.nz's citation for POL55077 (nutrition-guidelines review) points to an unrelated NZ First release (Mill Road); the correct party text is linked as well.

### POL54756: Complete the reconstruction of Christchurch Cathedral

**Statement:** Complete the reconstruction of Christchurch Cathedral  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: media-culture-and-recreation, law-justice-and-government, arts-culture-and-heritage, local-government

- **Why:** This party claims the rebuild is representative of Christchurch's earthquake recovery. Completing the rebuild would restore a symbol of the city's heritage and be a boost for local tourism and business in the city.
- **How:** The party has pledged $15m dollars to Christ Church Cathedral Reinstatement Ltd to complete the company's proposed pathway. The funding would be alongside money Christchurch City Council, not instead of. 

The additional government funding would help complete the first stage of the new rebuild project. This would re-open the Cathedral and remove the hoardings from the square during the first stage of full revitalisation.

 This party estimates that this policy would cost 15 million over one year.
- **Note:** policy.nz's second citation is the same release on community.scoop.co.nz.

**Statement:** Ban public sales of fireworks  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: law-justice-and-government, media-culture-and-recreation, family-justice-and-safety, sports-and-recreation

### POL54754: Increase the milk quantity guaranteed to NZ dairy manufacturing

**Statement:** Increase the milk quantity guaranteed to NZ dairy manufacturing  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: economy, agriculture, trade-and-exports, economic-development-and-industry

- **Why:** This party says that the present 50 million litres per year is too low to incentivise production at a large scale. The status-quo supports New Zealand-based dairy manufacturers, but does not support these firms to scale to size, which disincentives investment into Fonterra. 

Marketing ‘New Zealand Dairy’, this party sees this policy as a means of making NZ’s dairy manufacturing sector more competitive in export markets. It says it is important for the milk provision not to be a subsidy; dairy manufacturing firms would cover delivery and collection costs and pay farmers market rates.
- **How:** This party would increase milk access from 50 million litres to 500 million litres per year over the first six years. From there, access would taper to 80 per cent, 60 per cent, 40 per cent and 20 per cent to encourage immediate investment. - **Why:** This party says that student visa holders compete in the competitive graduate job market and can take jobs from New Zealanders. It stays the intent of international education is for overseas economies to give money to NZ by paying for their education, not to provide automatic work rights and residence pathways. ### NZF-A08: 'Life means life': degrees of murder, whole-of-life sentences for first-degree murder and child rape

**Statement:** 'Life means life': degrees of murder, whole-of-life sentences for first-degree murder and child rape  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice, law-justice-and-government

- **Why:** The party says the justice system too often fails to hold offenders to account and victims should come before offenders.
- **How:** This party would create a formal 'degrees of murder' regime (1st degree: life without parole; 2nd degree: minimum non-parole period of 30 years; 3rd degree: minimum 10 years), increase sentences for attempted murder and wounding with intent from 14 to 25 years, and introduce life imprisonment for rape of children.
- **Sources:**
  - [NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime (Press release, 2026-10-22)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm) — [full text](documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences.md)

### NZF-A09: More mandatory minimum sentences, tougher parole and limits on sentence discounts

**Statement:** More mandatory minimum sentences, tougher parole and limits on sentence discounts  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: criminal-justice

- **Why:** The party says sentencing has not delivered justice for victims.
- **How:** This party would increase the use of mandatory minimum sentences for serious violent and sexual offenders, cap non-guilty-plea discounts at 10% (guilty-plea discounts stay at 25%), raise parole eligibility to 75% of the sentence for long-term offenders, require murderers to be assessed as low risk before release, set an 8-year minimum non-parole period for 'coward punch' killings, treat home burglary like aggravated burglary, and oppose any extension of the Clean Slate law.
- **Sources:**
  - [NZFirst Law And Order Policy Announcement: Tougher Sentences, Degrees Of Murder, Smashing Organised Crime (Press release, 2026-10-22)](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA2610/S00200/nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences-degrees-of-murder-smashing-organised-crime.htm) — [full text](documents/2026-10-22-nzfirst-law-and-order-policy-announcement-tougher-sentences.md)

**Statement:** Create a National Energy Strategy and stop power companies holding back supply to raise prices  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: energy, prices

### NZF-A05: Set mining zones, longer permits, reopen the School of Mines and refocus the Department of Conservation

**Statement:** Set mining zones, longer permits, reopen the School of Mines and refocus the Department of Conservation  
*Summary source: archive* · topics: land-and-resources, economy, conservation, education

- **Why:** The party says mining rules are duplicated, slow and inconsistent and are stopping investment and jobs.
- **How:** As part of its mining package this party would identify mining zones with clearer rules, lengthen mining permits to cover the life of a mine including rehabilitation, reopen the School of Mines and fund trades training, fund Mines Rescue, invest in R&D for onshore value-add, refocus DOC on areas of high conservation value, review stewardship land, remove duplication including in the Wildlife Act, and make consultation time-bound.
- **Sources:**

# New Zealand Loyal (NZ Loyal) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **New Zealand Loyal (NZ Loyal)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **10 policies** listed, backed by **1 full-text source document** and 1 documented-as-unretrievable source.

- Party website: <https://nzloyal.com/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 (re-registered; Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

NZ Loyal (leader Kelvyn Alp) was re-registered in August 2026. **Its own policy pages could not be captured**: nzloyal.com is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge that blocked both curl and a headless browser. The only verbatim party wording available to this archive is a ten-point list RNZ quoted from the party's website on 12 October 2026; each point is listed below with that RNZ article as the source.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/nz-loyal/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Full policy text NOT retrievable (nzloyal.com HTTP 403 Cloudflare; web.archive.org unreachable from this environment; newzealandloyal.com is a parked domain). Detail behind each headline (mechanisms, costs) is unknown. A separate group calling itself the 'Real NZ Loyal' disputes Alp's leadership (reported by The Press and Wikipedia); this archive lists the registered party's stated policies only.

## Economy

### Adopt an 'Open Source First' rule for government software procurement (OFP-10)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says dependence on multinational software vendors is a hidden import cost and a resilience risk.

**How** (*archive*): Agencies must check for a suitable open-source option before buying proprietary software, compare whole-of-life costs, and use New Zealand providers for support.

Full text: [Open Source First: Keeping New Zealand' s Digital Wealth in New Zealand](documents/open-source-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/open-source-policy))

### Replace the fisheries Quota Management System with a LegaSea-style system keeping fisheries in public ownership (OFP-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the QMS has depleted fish stocks, privatised a public resource and priced locals out.

**How** (*archive*): Tendered commercial permits with no private sale of fishing rights, catches landed and processed in NZ, only NZ-owned operators, fleet separation in the territorial sea, and more recreational and customary inshore access.

Full text: [Fisheries Policy](documents/nzofp-fisheries-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/nzofp-fisheries-policy))

## Education

### Make early childhood centres and primary schools Wi-Fi free, using wired connections (OFP-15)

**How** (*archive*): Minimise Wi-Fi in high schools too and work with Chorus on wired fibre connections.

Full text: [Education Policy](documents/education-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/education-policy))

### Invest heavily in education with an outdoors- and community-focused curriculum, implementing the Tomorrow's Schools Review (OFP-16)

Full text: [Education Policy](documents/education-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/education-policy))

## Environment

### Withdraw from the Paris Agreement and focus on flood management and carbon-rich soils (OFP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says farm animals cannot release more carbon than they eat and that extreme weather is 'nature, not climate change'.

**How** (*archive*): Exit Paris (it says staying would cost more than leaving), maintain river flows and channels to reduce flood risk, and support ecological agriculture with minimal synthetic inputs.

Full text: [Agriculture Policy](documents/agriculture-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/agriculture-policy))

### Replace the EPA with an independent Health-Environment Protection Agency and apply the precautionary principle to new technology (OFP-05)

**How** (*archive*): New technologies and products only with full liability for the business introducing them; independent biosecurity at every entry point.

Full text: [Agriculture Policy](documents/agriculture-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/agriculture-policy))

### Replace DOC with a Department of Outdoors – Wildlife, Recreation & Nature (DOWRN) (OFP-18)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says governments have undervalued New Zealanders' outdoors culture and access.

**How** (*archive*): A department promoting access to all public land, coasts and rivers, poison-free conservation (trapping rather than poisons), food gathering on public land, and early public engagement on access decisions.

Full text: [Recreation & Wildlife Policy](documents/outdoors-recreation-and-wildlife-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/outdoors-recreation-and-wildlife-policy))

## Health

### Decriminalise personal cannabis use and cultivation and support medicinal cannabis and hemp (OFP-11)

**How** (*archive*): No criminal offence for personal possession or growing; support home-grown medicinal cannabis and small NZ suppliers over 'Big Pharma', with lower licensing barriers; update law to support hemp products.

Full text: [Cannabis Policy](documents/cannabis-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/cannabis-policy))

### Create a nationwide anti-bullying strategy treating bullying as a public-health issue (OFP-12)

**How** (*archive*): Awareness programmes in schools and communities, leadership training for teachers and managers, bullying questions in routine health screening, and treatment of psychological effects.

Full text: [Anti Bullying Policy](documents/anti-bullying-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/anti-bullying-policy))

### Make one doctor's injury diagnosis final for ACC and abolish ACC's review and dispute machinery (OFP-13)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says ACC 'expert shopping' is used to decline claims.

**How** (*archive*): Disestablish ACC review specialists and investigators, cancel contracts with FairWay and ICRA, stop paying external consultants to contest diagnoses; it claims $61.5m a year savings to redirect to surgery, rehabilitation and disability support.

Full text: [ACC Policy Statement](documents/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement))

### Pursue Pfizer for breach of contract over Covid-19 vaccines and recover ACC vaccine-injury costs (OFP-14)

**How** (*archive*): Release the full NZ Pfizer contract, bring a Crown claim to recover the $16.8m ACC has paid for vaccine injuries, guarantee ACC compensation for long-term vaccine harm, give ACC a statutory right of recourse against manufacturers, and review ACC law to cover distress and loss of enjoyment of life.

Full text: [ACC Policy Statement](documents/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/the-acc-justice-accountability-policy-statement))

## Housing

### Free up land and revise the RMA to speed house building, with a mix of public and private housing (OFP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says every citizen should have access to an affordable, warm, dry home.

**How** (*archive*): Identify land for subdivision, sequence servicing and construction, and have the Ministry of Housing take a hands-on role.

Full text: [Housing Policy](documents/housing-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/housing-policy))

### Require high standards for new homes (R5 insulation, rainwater and greywater systems, energy efficiency) and fund hempcrete building (OFP-08)

**How** (*archive*): Also solar or micro-generation, green space for gardens, recycling of building materials, lower consent costs for sustainable materials, and a funding scheme for hempcrete homes.

Full text: [Housing Policy](documents/housing-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/housing-policy))

### Fully fund night shelters and low-cost living spaces for homeless people (OFP-09)

**How** (*archive*): Shelters would provide two nutritious meals a day and supplements; the party also wants to restore New Zealand's leadership in social housing.

Full text: [Housing Policy](documents/housing-policy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/housing-policy))

## Law, justice & government

### Entrench the NZ Bill of Rights Act as supreme law (OFP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says Covid-era measures showed fundamental rights could be overridden by a simple parliamentary majority and that select-committee consultation is 'a toothless illusion'.

**How** (*archive*): Make the Bill of Rights the constitutional bedrock so no government or emergency declaration can override rights such as free speech, movement, assembly and the right to refuse medical treatment.

Full text: [DIRECT DEMOcracy](documents/direct-democracy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/direct-democracy))

### Introduce Swiss-style binding citizens' referendums: a citizens' veto on laws and citizen-initiated laws (OFP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says Covid-era measures showed fundamental rights could be overridden by a simple parliamentary majority and that select-committee consultation is 'a toothless illusion'.

**How** (*archive*): Citizens could gather signatures to force a binding nationwide vote to strike down a law, or to put their own draft law on the ballot, with a lower signature threshold than the current 10% for non-binding referendums.

Full text: [DIRECT DEMOcracy](documents/direct-democracy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/direct-democracy))

### Decentralise government under a 'subsidiarity' principle and let regions keep part of the GST and tax raised locally (OFP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says Covid-era measures showed fundamental rights could be overridden by a simple parliamentary majority and that select-committee consultation is 'a toothless illusion'.

**How** (*archive*): Return decisions on local infrastructure, land management and regional development to communities, shrink central ministries and give regions financial autonomy.

Full text: [DIRECT DEMOcracy](documents/direct-democracy.md) ([original](https://freedom.kiwi/direct-democracy))

# Opportunity (The Opportunity Party, TOP) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Opportunity (The Opportunity Party, TOP)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **77 policies** listed (56 from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/opportunity-party), 21 added by this archive from the party's own documents), backed by **64 full-text source documents** and 3 documented-as-unretrievable sources.

- Party website: <https://www.opportunity.org.nz/>
- Registration: 6 March 2017 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

Opportunity (leader Qiulae Wong) publishes its platform as 15 policy pages (priority policies: Abundant Energy, Breakthrough Economy, Clean Up Politics, Healthy Oceans, Tax Reset; plus Citizens' Voice, Future-fit Education, Healthy People, Honouring Te Tiriti, Smart on Crime, Affordable Housing, Digital Future, Inter-Generational Infrastructure, Climate Action, Healthy Land & Water), most with a downloadable PDF policy paper, plus statements and five election "bottom lines". The list below starts from policy.nz's 56 statements for the party (with policy.nz's own Why/How text) and adds policies from TOP's documents that policy.nz does not list (IDs OPP-A..).

**How the text was obtained.** www.opportunity.org.nz is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (HTTP 403 to curl and headless Chromium) and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment, so web pages were recovered from **Common Crawl** WARC captures (crawls CC-MAIN-2026-30/34/39/43; capture date in each document's front matter) via [`tools/policies_minor_cc.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_cc.py). The 15 policy PDFs were downloaded directly from cdn.opportunity.org.nz (not blocked). Press releases are also taken from their scoop.co.nz mirrors.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/opportunity/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

Summaries marked *policy.nz* are policy.nz's neutral "This party says…" text, reproduced unchanged. Summaries marked *archive* were written for this archive from the linked full text: one to three neutral sentences; "Why" is the party's own stated reason, "How" what it says it would do.

**Gaps and caveats.** Three pages cited by policy.nz have no Common Crawl capture and could not be retrieved: /healthy_land (Healthy Land & Water policy — water quality, gene technology context), /disability_statement and /arts_and_culture_statement; their documents say so explicitly, and the policy.nz summaries are kept. Common Crawl captures date from July–October 2026 and may predate later edits. Note that the Citizens' Voice PDF is dated June 2025. The NZ Herald reported (Oct 2026) that tax reform is not among TOP's five bottom lines; the Tax Reset remains on its policy page. Web search capacity ran out during research, so further Scoop mirrors were not sought.

## Community & inclusion

### Support the online safety bill on a potential under-16 social media ban to select committee (POL54783)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that it is concerned about the effects of social media on those under 16, and supports a discussion on whether to impose a ban. However, it adds that an age restriction is not a substitute for stronger obligations on social media companies to address digital harm.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would support National’s online safety bill at first reading so it can be properly tested at select committee. It will wait for the select committee to examine the evidence before taking a position on the effectiveness of a social media ban for young people.

Full text: ['Opportunity to support online safety bill to select committee', 25 August 2026 (accessed 28 August 2026)](documents/web-opportunity-to-support-online-safety-bill-to-select-committee.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/opportunity_to_support_online_safety_bill_to_select_committee))

### Bring in tougher rules around tobacco, vaping, alcohol, and unhealthy food (POL54885)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that tobacco, alcohol and unhealthy food account for roughly a quarter of all the healthy years New Zealanders lose to death and disability. Prevention receives a small fraction of health spending relative to the share of health loss these risks cause.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would work to reduce the harm from tobacco, as well as alcohol and unhealthy food, as part of a 10-year health plan. This would include a renewed Smoke-free New Zealand programme, with fewer places selling tobacco, and mandated de-nicotinisation of smoked tobacco. 
Quit programmes and regulated alternatives for adult smokers would be better funded, and there would be stronger protections against youth access to vapes.

Full text: ['Healthy People ', undated (accessed 19 August 2026)](documents/web-healthy-people.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/healthy_people))

### Restore pay equity deals for care and support workers (POL55265)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that recent law changes cancelled many active pay equity claims. This included disability care and support workers, and experts warn this will make it harder to hire and keep workers, cause staff shortages, and lower the quality of care.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would re-instate rules from the Equal Pay Amendment Act 2020 to ensure care and support workers get fairer pay and recognise their skills, helping to create a stable, long-lasting care workforce.

Full text: ['Who's listening to our disability advocates? ', undated (accessed 19 August 2026)](documents/web-who-s-listening-to-our-disability-advocates.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/who_s_listening_to_our_disability_advocates)); ['Disability Statement', 12 October 2026 (accessed 12 October 2026)](documents/web-disability-statement.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/disability_statement))

### Improved respite and carer support for the disabled (POL55267)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says accessibility and care is a growing issue. One in six Kiwis have a disability and if ageing-related access issues are factored in, 1 in 4 Kiwis will have accessibility needs in their lifetimes. Everyone should be able to participate in society with dignity and make the most of opportunities. However, the current Disability Support Services Bill did not properly consult with those it affects, and fails to give paid and unpaid carers the support they deserve.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would look to improve disability policy, including good care plans for disabled adults as their family carers age. It would back pay equity for care and support workers. It would also seek more support for unpaid carers, with improved respite care and more flexibility to balance their employment and unpaid caring roles.

Full text: ['Disability Statement', 12 October 2026 (accessed 12 October 2026)](documents/web-disability-statement.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/disability_statement)); ['Who's listening to our disability advocates? ', undated (accessed 19 August 2026)](documents/web-who-s-listening-to-our-disability-advocates.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/who_s_listening_to_our_disability_advocates))

### Oppose disabled people being paid less than minimum wage (POL55269)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that many disabled people lose benefit income if they work and some are even legally paid less than the minimum wage. One in six Kiwis are disabled and when ageing-related access issues are factored in, one in four Kiwis will face access issues in their lifetimes. So access to care and income are key issues for those with disabilities.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would work to end rules that allow disabled people to be paid less than the minimum wage. It would improve support for employers to recruit and retain disabled workers. This party argues its Citizens’ Income and Disability Allowance would ensure disabled people would not lose income support for doing paid work.

Full text: ['Disability Statement', 12 October 2026 (accessed 12 October 2026)](documents/web-disability-statement.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/disability_statement)); ['Who's listening to our disability advocates? ', undated (accessed 19 August 2026)](documents/web-who-s-listening-to-our-disability-advocates.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/who_s_listening_to_our_disability_advocates))

### Ensure better connections between government systems and those with a disability (POL55271)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says people with long-term disabilities often find themselves endlessly repeating their story or having to prove their disability to authorities. Or they may fall through the cracks if their health, education, ACC and disability support systems are not strongly connected.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would back a "Tell Us Once" system, which would mean those with long-term disability support needs would not have to repeat their story or have tests over and over. Privacy would be protected and they would have control over how their information was shared. They would be supported to navigate the various government agencies that are connected to their case.

## Economy

### Increase innovation by lifting science funding to 2 percent of GDP (POL54779)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that economic growth is slowing and new ideas are needed in the areas of science and technology.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would increase innovation by lifting science funding to 2 percent of GDP. It would also turn polytechs into regional innovation hubs, offer incentives to invest in technology and beef up proven accelerator programmes. The wider innovation plan would cost an additional $1.33bn but create $4bn revenue annually.

Full text: ['Breakthrough Economy', undated (accessed 19 August 2026)](documents/web-breakthrough-economy.md) ([original](https://www.opportunity.org.nz/breakthrough-economy)); ['Breakthrough Economy Overview' (PDF), 1 July 2026 (accessed 19 August 2026)](documents/pdf-breakthrough-economy.md) ([original](https://cdn.opportunity.org.nz/documents/policy/breakthrough-economy-policy-overview.pdf)); [Innovation, Fairness And Small Business: Opportunity’s Breakthrough Economy Policy](documents/release-2026-07-breakthrough-economy.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2607/S00015/innovation-fairness-and-small-business-opportunitys-breakthrough-economy-policy.htm)); [Digital Future (policy document)](documents/pdf-digital-future.md) ([original](https://cdn.opportunity.org.nz/documents/policy/Opportunity%20Policy%20-%20Digital%20Future.pdf))

### Enforce and fund a 30-year infrastructure plan (POL54785)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that short-term political cycles have led to wastage and a lack of planning for long-term infrastructure.  It notes New Zealand compares badly against most OECD countries for maintaining its existing assets. Te Waihanga, the Infrastructure Commission, could be given a greater role to ensure that major projects continue between governments.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would lock into law the 30-year National Infrastructure Plan published by Te Waihanga, which would also be put in charge of the funding and delivery of projects. Major projects, where the government is investing over $250m, would require a bill through Parliament to cancel. This policy would cost around $27 million annually for the enhanced infrastructure commission and ties in with a $150m free public transport policy and a $60bn infrastructure capital fund.

Full text: ['Intergenerational Infrastructure' (PDF), undated (accessed 11 August 2026)](documents/pdf-intergenerational-infrastructure.md) ([original](https://cdn.opportunity.org.nz/documents/policy/intergenerational-infrastructure.pdf)); [Intergenerational Infrastructure (policy document)](documents/pdf-intergenerational-infrastructure.md) ([original](https://cdn.opportunity.org.nz/documents/policy/Opportunity%20Policy%20-%20Intergenerational%20Infrastructure.pdf)); [Opportunity Launches Intergenerational Infrastructure Policy](documents/release-2026-08-intergenerational-infrastructure.md) ([original](https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2608/S00027/opportunity-launches-intergenerational-infrastructure-policy.htm))

### Give councils more tools to invest in infrastructure (POL54811)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says local authorities have been forced to rely almost entirely on property rates to service ageing infrastructure under growing demand. New tools are needed to help them maintain these assets and build new ones.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would ensure councils had access to more tools such as congestion charges, value capture and accommodation levies and user-pays charges to help fund infrastructure. Funds would also be available through housing funds, climate resilience funds and council-specific loans.  A 30 percent cap on the Uniform Annual General Charge would also be repealed. 
Council spending would be overseen by an expanded Infrastructure Commission.

### Phase out inshore bottom-trawling by 2030 and make fishing more sustainable (POL54776)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that our seas are hitting their ecological and economic limits. Fish species are being depleted under the current quota management system, and critical habitats are unprotected. Just 0.5% of NZ’s extensive ocean territory is protected as a marine reserve.

## Housing

### Introduce a land value tax of 1.75 percent (POL54777)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that the current tax system is outdated and does not address the cost-of-living crisis, unaffordable housing, and the increasing pressure of the superannuation system. Under its tax plan, this party says incomes will increase for 70 percent of New Zealanders, and another 20% will see no change.

**How** (*policy.nz*): An annual land value tax of 1.75 percent on urban land - and 0.5% on rural land - would be part of a wider tax reset aimed at incomes, house prices and retirement savings. The land value tax would lower house prices an estimated 10-15 percent and discourage land-banking and large property portfolios. There would be potential exemptions for farmers, retirees and other "land rich, cash poor" land owners. 
This tax would fund a universal citizen's income, with an extra $4bn for other uses. The tax system would also be simplified, with the number of tax brackets reduced to three - 28 percent, 34 percent and 39 percent

## Media, culture & recreation

### Provide more support for the arts through a citizens income and innovation funding (POL55323)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that a stronger arts ecosystem creates jobs and wellbeing, builds healthier communities and helps define national identity. NZ sits in the bottom ten OECD countries for public arts investment. The barriers for artists are less about a lack of arts funding and more about unpredictable income, and changing a mindset that the arts are a key part of the economy, rather than an optional extra.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would address the precarity of an artist's income firstly with its universal citizen’s income policy, which would enable artists to take a financial gamble on their career. Tax reforms would help over irregular income and free up charitable giving by repealing the cap on charitable donations. This party would more broadly support the arts through other policies such as an AI framework and revamp of the polytech sector, which would address copyright exploitation and recognise the arts in innovation funding.

## Transport & infrastructure

### Increase incentives to electrify houses, industries and transport (POL54770)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says New Zealand has solar, wind, hydro and geothermal resources but continues to rely too heavily on fossil fuels. It says increasing renewable energy and promoting the electrification household and industry electrification would have many benefits such as increased GDP, lower carbon emissions, smaller power bills and 5,000 new jobs over the next 30 years.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would incentivise the electrification of industries and housing. This would include an expansion of EECA’s Warmer Kiwi Homes subsidies ($80m annually) for household solar and electricity initiatives, and low-interest electrification loans via the national Ratepayer Assistance Scheme.

### Increase the energy grid up to 30GW by 2050 (POL54807)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says New Zealand has solar, wind, hydro and geothermal resources but continues to rely too heavily on fossil fuels. Increasing renewable energy and promoting the electrification of households and industries would have many benefits such as increased GDP, lower carbon emissions, smaller power bills and 5,000 new jobs over the next 30 years.

### Offer incentives to businesses to buy electric vehicles (POL54876)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says encouraging businesses to buy electric vehicles will reduce their ongoing fuel costs and make them more resilient to volatile prices. As businesses are big buyers of new vehicles, this would also increase the pool of EVs in the secondhand market.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would allow accelerated depreciation and fringe benefit tax exemptions for business electric vehicles worth up to $50,000 (or $75,000 for utes and vans).
The fringe benefit tax exemption is expected to cost $31m a year, growing to $155m as uptake increases. 
The impact of accelerated depreciation will start at about $95m a year, but much of it will be recovered as depreciation timing unwinds. Both will be funded from ringfenced dividends from state gentailers.

### Help industries decarbonise with a new fund (POL54900)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that electrification of industry is being blocked by the cost of plant capital, grid connection and network upgrades. Industry has been hampered by a fall in gas reserves and the scrapping of GIDI, a government industry decarbonisation fund. A replacement loan guarantee scheme has fallen short because it cannot overcome the upfront cost, debt constraints and investment risks. This party says money collected from selling carbon units should be used to fight climate pollution, not disappear into the government's consolidated fund.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would establish a ring-fenced Industry Energy Resilience Fund (IERF) which would cover capital and upgrade costs. The fund will be capitalised by a $1b green bond raised against forecast ETS auction revenues over the next decade. 
IERF will offer a greater mix of instruments than GIDI , with grants reserved for smaller targeted uses. 
Money collected from selling carbon units would be used to fight climate change, putting it into IERF by law so businesses could plan ahead.

### Use the money received from stakes in gentailers to fund renewable energy (POL55049)

**Why** (*policy.nz*): This party says that New Zealand has solar, wind, hydro and geothermal resources but continues to rely too heavily on fossil fuels. It says increasing renewable energy and promoting the electrification household and industry electrification would have many benefits. The current electricity system is unfair; renewable energy generation has been underfunded and created expensive power bills for individuals and businesses. The government has a majority stake in several major power companies and is incentivised to keep prices high.

**How** (*policy.nz*): This party would add 30 gigawatts of renewable energy to the grid by 2050. This ambitious target will require building just over 556 megawatts of electricity generation to the country every year. The government currently receives approximately $500m from stakes in the electricity gentailers each year. This money would be ringfenced for investment in generation so that there is no incentive to maintain high prices. Electricity distributors would be consolidated and all electricity regulation would fall under one regulator. This party estimates that this policy would cost 500 m.

# Progressive Aotearoa New Zealand (Progressive Party, PPANZ) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Progressive Aotearoa New Zealand (Progressive Party, PPANZ)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **14 policies** listed, backed by **2 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/>
- Registration: Not a registered party; electorate candidates only (Nelson: Bruce Dyer; West Coast-Tasman: Kevin Rooke; Kāpiti: Michael Walker — per policy.nz)

## About this list

The Progressive Party (PPANZ) publishes a 'Policies' page with sections on health, housing, education, justice, Māori policy, animals and plants, agriculture, climate change, industry, taxation and social boards, each beginning 'The Progressive Party advocates…', plus a longer 'PPANZ Manifesto' (marked as a work in progress, including a Covid-19 strategy white paper). The main advocated positions are listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/progressive-aotearoa-new-zealand/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** Undated pages; no costings. The manifesto is captured in full but its points largely repeat the Policies page.

## Headline policies

- [Guarantee access to food, clothing, housing, education and healthcare](#guarantee-access-to-food-clothing-housing-education-and-healthcare-ppa-01) — Community & inclusion
- [Offer state-funded mortgages, a state-owned house-building enterprise and limit home ownership to NZ residents](#offer-state-funded-mortgages-a-state-owned-house-building-enterprise-and-limit-home-ownership-to-nz-residents-ppa-04) — Housing
- [Run businesses with more than nine employees as worker co-operatives and state-manage monopolistic key industries](#run-businesses-with-more-than-nine-employees-as-worker-co-operatives-and-state-manage-monopolistic-key-industries-ppa-12) — Economy

## Contents by topic

- [Community & inclusion](#community--inclusion) (1)
- [Economy](#economy) (2)
- [Education](#education) (1)
- [Environment](#environment) (2)
- [Health](#health) (2)
- [Housing](#housing) (1)
- [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (1)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (2)
- [Te ao Māori](#te-ao-māori) (2)

## Community & inclusion

### Guarantee access to food, clothing, housing, education and healthcare (PPA-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The Progressive Party says economic and political power should serve people rather than concentrated wealth (its stated philosophy draws on economic democracy and 'neohumanism').

**How** (*archive*): Listed in the health, housing and education sections as guarantees for everyone.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Economy

### Shift farming to co-operatives and plant-based protein (PPA-10)

**How** (*archive*): Incentivise farmers to move to plant protein (including lab-grown meat) and regenerative, ethical farming models; co-operatives at all levels of agriculture.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Run businesses with more than nine employees as worker co-operatives and state-manage monopolistic key industries (PPA-12)

**How** (*archive*): A Minister, Ministry and Centre for Cooperative Studies; railways, power and mining state-managed; a nationwide co-operative supermarket to cut living costs.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Education

### Move schooling from national standards to child-centred, experiential learning including meditation and mindfulness (PPA-07)

**How** (*archive*): Learning based on each child's needs, parents as active partners, restorative behaviour management and a Hauora (holistic wellbeing) approach.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Environment

### Establish a Ministry for Animal and Plant Welfare and extend legal advocacy to nature (PPA-09)

**How** (*archive*): Building on Te Urewera's legal personhood and animals' legal recognition as sentient.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Build a government-backed renewables industry and prepare to move infrastructure 10 metres above sea level (PPA-11)

**How** (*archive*): Electrify transport, convert sewage and organic waste to biogas and biodiesel, raise eco-housing standards, phase out gas appliances, and redirect foreign aid toward emissions cuts in the Pacific.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Health

### Create an independent National Health Board outside the Health Ministry to oversee Te Whatu Ora (PPA-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says this would counterbalance political influence on health priorities.

**How** (*archive*): A board of health experts with elected and appointed members, plus co-operative primary and residential care, Māori-for-Māori services and higher taxes on harmful products ring-fenced for health.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Legalise cannabis as a health issue and support the End-of-Life Choice Act (PPA-03)

**How** (*archive*): Tax revenue from cannabis would go to health, with research on benefits and harms; the party also lists voluntary vaccination and a review of Covid-era measures for future pandemics.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Housing

### Offer state-funded mortgages, a state-owned house-building enterprise and limit home ownership to NZ residents (PPA-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says leaving housing to the market 'amounts to a dereliction of duty'.

**How** (*archive*): Also long-term leasing, co-operative housing and co-housing options, and a capital gains tax to curb speculation.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Incomes & employment

### Phase out income tax in favour of taxes on production, remove GST from fresh produce and introduce a capital gains tax (PPA-13)

**How** (*archive*): Income tax would become a mechanism capping salaries at a maximum linked to the minimum wage, set by a Wages and Salary Commission.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Law, justice & government

### Focus prisons on rehabilitation, education and restorative justice, and end for-profit prisons (PPA-08)

**Why** (*archive*): The party views crime as rooted in social and economic conditions.

**How** (*archive*): Skills training and tikanga Māori in prisons, mental-health services, restorative justice, community reintegration support, and terminating private prison arrangements.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Create Social Boards of respected community members to advise local and national government (PPA-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says they would moderate lobby groups' influence.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

## Te ao Māori

### Make te reo Māori compulsory in primary and secondary schools, aiming for a bilingual Aotearoa (PPA-05)

**How** (*archive*): Language parity with English, plus full teaching of New Zealand history and the constitutional documents (Te Tiriti and He Whakaputanga).

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))

### Entrench the Māori seats in Parliament (PPA-06)

**How** (*archive*): Give the Māori seats the same entrenched protection as general seats.

Full text: [Policies](documents/policies.md) ([original](https://www.progressiveparty.co.nz/policies-3/))
