# Te Pāti Māori — 2026 election policies

Every 2026 policy of Te Pāti Māori that this archive could find, with a short neutral summary (**Why** — the reason the party gives; **How** — what it would do) and links to the **full verbatim text** of the party's own documents in [`documents/`](documents/). Election day: 7 November 2026. Compiled 23 October 2026.

## At a glance

- **91 policies** listed: 45 from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz) (all of its 45 Te Pāti Māori statements, with its Why/How summaries) + 46 more found in the party's own releases, speeches and policy PDFs (marked *archive*; summaries written for this archive).
- **68 full-text documents** archived (24 party web pages via Common Crawl, 23 press releases/speeches via Scoop, 21 PDFs) + 1 placeholder file(s) for cited pages that could not be retrieved.
- 91 policies have at least one retrieved party text; 0 rely only on a page that could not be retrieved.

## Method & sources

1. Started from policy.nz's Te Pāti Māori data (`raw/policy.nz/parties/te-pati-maori.json`): statement, Why/How, citations.
2. maoriparty.org.nz blocks automated access (Cloudflare 403, also with a headless browser) and web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment. The party's own web pages were therefore recovered from **Common Crawl**: its 2026 crawl indexes (CC-MAIN-2026-12 … -43) were searched for every maoriparty.org.nz URL and the latest HTTP-200 capture of each page was read from the WARC archive on data.commoncrawl.org (`tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_index.py`, `tools/policies_nzf_tpm_cc_fetch.py`). Each such document (`documents/site-*.md`) records the capture date and WARC record; captures date from 2026-03-17 to 2026-10-08, so later edits are not reflected.
3. In addition, every Te Pāti Māori press release and speech from late 2025 to 23 Oct 2026 was collected from Scoop's organisation page (https://info.scoop.co.nz/Te_Pati_Maori); Scoop republishes party releases as issued, so their text is the party's own. Policy PDFs the party attached to releases (img.scoop.co.nz) or linked from its site (Google Drive) were downloaded and text-extracted.
4. Each policy links (a) the page policy.nz cited (now mostly a Common Crawl capture) and (b) other party texts on the same policy. Where a cited page could not be recovered at all, a `documents/not-retrieved-*.md` file records the URL and the reason; it contains no paraphrase.
5. Policies found in party texts but missing from policy.nz were added with neutral summaries (`summary_source: archive`). Calls on the current government and positions (e.g. opposing a bill) are included where the party presents them as what it stands for, and are labelled as such.

### Retrieval gaps (read this)

- **1 maoriparty.org.nz pages cited by policy.nz were not retrieved** (403 / archive unreachable). Where a party release covers the same policy it is linked, but the website page may contain details the release does not.
  - ['Sports', undated (accessed 18 August 2026)](documents/not-retrieved-maoriparty-sports.md) — <https://www.maoriparty.org.nz/sports> (policies: POL55068)
- The party's web policy pages are short summaries ("What we’ll do / Why it matters") that link to full manifesto chapters on Google Drive. Chapters recovered (all text-extracted in `documents/pdf-*.md`): Tax, Te Tiriti Entrenchment, Energy Sovereignty, Kai Sovereignty, Justice, Mana Motuhake, Military Neutrality, Climate, Toi Māori, Freshwater, Housing, Mokopuna Māori, Te Reo Māori, Mana Takatāpui. **No full chapter was linked for Health, Disabilities, Education & Training, Economic development or Cost of living** (those web pages have no Drive link in their captures); for these the web-page summary and the party's “What matters to you?” tool (which says its content is from the Policy Manifesto 2026) are the fullest party texts found.
- The site's Sports and Disability pages link to older documents (a 2020 sport policy; a 2023 Mana Hauā policy). They are archived but flagged as not 2026 policy.
- maoriparty.org.nz/sports (cited by policy.nz) has no Common Crawl capture; the policy index page (captured 8 Oct 2026) includes the same Sports summary.
- No Te Pāti Māori statement of formal coalition "bottom lines" was found. Its stated strategy is a candidate vote for Te Pāti Māori and party vote for Labour or the Greens, aiming for a one-term government.

## Headline commitments & stated conditions

- **Electoral strategy:** “Candidate vote Te Pāti Māori. Party vote Green or Labour, you choose.” The party list has one candidate (General Secretary Lance Norman) beyond its seven Māori electorate candidates. — [source](documents/2026-10-04-te-pati-maori-puts-its-money-where-its-mouth-is-with-one-per.md)
- **Goal:** “Our strategy is clear. We want more Māori in Parliament, a one-term Government, and an independent Māori voice that is accountable to our people.” — [source](documents/2026-10-04-te-pati-maori-puts-its-money-where-its-mouth-is-with-one-per.md)
- **Constitutional reform:** “Te Tiriti is the constitutional foundation of Aotearoa. Its mana does not rise and fall depending on who forms the Government.” — Entrenchment policy: binding Waitangi Tribunal recommendations, a Te Tiriti Commission with compliance-order powers, a $220m Mātike Mai Fund, UNDRIP action plan within 100 days. — [source](documents/2026-09-01-te-pati-maori-launches-te-tiriti-entrenchment-policy.md)
- **Tax:** Kiwi Tax Plan: first $30,000 tax-free, top rate 48% over $300,000, wealth tax from 1.5% above $2m net wealth, company tax back to 33%. (NZ First's leader said Te Pāti Māori called its tax policy a “bottom line”; this archive could not retrieve a Te Pāti Māori statement using that phrase.) — [source](documents/pdf-a-kiwi-tax-plan.md)

**Signature policies:** [Make the first $30,000 earned tax-free](#pol54812-make-the-first-30000-earned-tax-free); [Implement a targeted wealth tax starting from 1.5 percent](#pol54939-implement-a-targeted-wealth-tax-starting-from-15-percent); [Remove GST costs from kai](#pol54938-remove-gst-costs-from-kai); [Establish an independent Te Tiriti Commission](#pol54917-establish-an-independent-te-tiriti-commission); [Make Waitangi Tribunal recommendations binding](#pol54795-make-waitangi-tribunal-recommendations-binding); [Establish a $220 million Mātike Mai Fund and set 2040 as the target for constitutional transformation](#tpm-a03-establish-a-220-million-mātike-mai-fund-and-set-2040-as-the-target-for-constitutional-transformation); [Create a Māori Education Authority with responsibility for Māori education](#pol54679-create-a-māori-education-authority-with-responsibility-for-māori-education); [Invest in Māori energy sovereignty](#pol55059-invest-in-māori-energy-sovereignty); [Abolish prisons by 2040](#pol55283-abolish-prisons-by-2040); [Create an independent Māori Justice Authority funded from half of the Corrections, Police and Courts budgets](#tpm-a13-create-an-independent-māori-justice-authority-funded-from-half-of-the-corrections-police-and-courts-budgets); [Declare NZ a "military neutral" country](#pol54684-declare-nz-a-military-neutral-country); [Ban seabed mining](#pol54680-ban-seabed-mining); [$200 million over three years and an independent Takatāpui-governed Commission](#tpm-a12-200-million-over-three-years-and-an-independent-takatāpui-governed-commission); [Te Kōhanga Reo Act, secure baseline funding and 20 new kōhanga reo](#tpm-a08-te-kōhanga-reo-act-secure-baseline-funding-and-20-new-kōhanga-reo).

*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: environment, te-ao-maori, climate-adaptation, land-and-resources

### POL55059: Invest in Māori energy sovereignty

**Statement:** Invest in Māori energy sovereignty  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: transport-and-infrastructure, environment, te-ao-maori, energy, climate-adaptation, te-tiriti-o-waitangi-and-governance

- **Why:** This party says that currently energy production extracts wealth and autonomy from Māori. An energy transition must uphold tino rangatiratanga and give Māori tangible rights surrounding, and ownership of, energy
- **How:** This party would establish a $1b energy sovereignty fund. It will invest in energy resilience on marae, papakāinga, and Māori land more generally. It will also reduce household power costs and provide workforce development opportunities, with an end goal of allowing whānau, iwi, and more to own more energy assets.

### POL55060: Establish a national energy independence plan

**Statement:** Establish a national energy independence plan  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: transport-and-infrastructure, environment, energy, emissions-reduction

- **Why:** This party says that electricity and electricity generation increasingly is carried out by large corporations focused on profits, not people. It's important to create a pathway to energy independence away from monopolies.
- **How:** This party would create an independent national energy plan. It would implement a fairness framework to regulate power prices, and also identify where the renewable energies are required for a transition to cleaner energy. ### POL55283: Abolish prisons by 2040

**Statement:** Abolish prisons by 2040  
*Summary source: policy.nz* · topics: law-justice-and-government, te-ao-maori, criminal-justice, te-reo-maori-and-culture

- **Why:** This party says that young Māori are regularly criminalised early in their lives, and even once they get out, often end up re-offending. ### POL54921: Convene a Māori constitutional convention as laid out in Matike Mai

**Statement:** Convene a Māori constitutional convention as laid out in Matike Mai

The Mātike Mai project, which was founded in 2010 to strengthen the independence of iwi and hapū, is underfunded to resource such a transition.

# Te Tai Tokerau Party — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Te Tai Tokerau Party** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **22 policies** listed, backed by **1 full-text source document**.

- Party website: <https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/>
- Registration: 5 August 2026 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Te Tai Tokerau Party was launched by Te Tai Tokerau MP Mariameno Kapa-Kingi in May 2026 after her split from Te Pāti Māori. Its whole platform is published on one page, "TTP Pātaka Policy", organised in five pillars (Whānau, Whare, Whenua, Tino Rangatiratanga, Ōhanga Ā-Rohe). Each named policy on that page is listed below. The page does not give costings except where noted.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/te-tai-tokerau-party/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The "Tai Tokerau Fund" policy is marked by the party as "in development". No separate PDFs, press releases or costings were found on the site.

## Headline policies

- [Pass Te Ture Mokopuna (the Mokopuna Act) requiring government decisions to consider current and future generations of mokopuna](#pass-te-ture-mokopuna-the-mokopuna-act-requiring-government-decisions-to-consider-current-and-future-generations-of-mokopuna-ttp-01) — Community & inclusion
- [Wipe low-income whānau debt to MSD and IRD and replace the benefit system with a Universal Whānau Allowance](#wipe-low-income-whānau-debt-to-msd-and-ird-and-replace-the-benefit-system-with-a-universal-whānau-allowance-ttp-03) — Incomes & employment
- [Constitutionally protect He Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti, and repeal the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 and the Treaty Clauses Review](#constitutionally-protect-he-whakaputanga-and-te-tiriti-and-repeal-the-regulatory-standards-act-2025-and-the-treaty-clauses-review-ttp-13) — Te ao Māori

## Contents by topic

- [Community & inclusion](#community--inclusion) (2)
- [Economy](#economy) (3)
- [Environment](#environment) (4)
- [Health](#health) (1)
- [Housing](#housing) (1)
- [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (3)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (2)
- [Te ao Māori](#te-ao-māori) (6)

## Community & inclusion

### Pass Te Ture Mokopuna (the Mokopuna Act) requiring government decisions to consider current and future generations of mokopuna (TTP-01)

**Why** (*archive*): The party calls this its flagship policy, modelled on Wales's Well-being of Future Generations Act 2015 and grounded in mātauranga Māori and Te Tiriti.

**How** (*archive*): Public bodies would be bound by a 'Mokopuna Principle', report annually against mokopuna wellbeing goals, carry out Mokopuna Impact Assessments on significant laws, Budgets and projects, and be monitored by an independent Commissioner for Mokopuna using co-designed national indicators.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Provide free solar power, home-delivered kai and paid cultural roles for kaumātua (TTP-07)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says many kaumātua live in energy poverty and are cut off from whānau and tribal roles.

**How** (*archive*): Prioritise elder-occupied homes for fully funded solar and batteries on community grids with zero-cost baseline electricity; monthly fresh-food prescription vouchers delivered to homes; paid mentorship roles for kaumātua and kuia; and paid, trained in-home carers drawn from local whānau ('Ringa Manaaki Dividend').

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Economy

### Build Local Business Incubators in Whangārei, Kaikohe and Kaitaia with a five-year 100% tax holiday for start-ups (TTP-19)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says young people leave the North because it lacks high-spec commercial infrastructure.

**How** (*archive*): Funded co-working spaces with fibre, fabrication labs and studios; businesses based in the incubators would pay no 'regional corporate income tax' for five years if local payroll and staffing targets are met; plus mentoring and seed grants.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Require government agencies to buy 10% (rising to 15% by 2030) of goods and services from Māori-owned and local businesses (TTP-20)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says state money spent in the regions should stay there.

**How** (*archive*): A 'Social & Indigenous Procurement Mandate' for schools, hospitals and construction, a 35% local Māori employment and 50% youth/apprenticeship target on regional projects, and 'Farm to School' purchasing of Māori-grown food.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Create a Tai Tokerau Fund modelled on the Provincial Growth Fund, specific to iwi (details in development) (TTP-22)

**How** (*archive*): The party lists a regional, iwi-specific fund modelled on the Provincial Growth Fund; its page says full detail is still in development.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Environment

### Set up a $150m-a-year Kaitiaki Guardians Network with statutory environmental enforcement powers (TTP-09)

**Why** (*archive*): The party wants Māori to move from being 'consulted' on the environment to being its legal 'eyes and ears'.

**How** (*archive*): A $150 million annual Crown appropriation for iwi- and hapū-led guardian teams with statutory power to monitor and enforce environmental rules in their rohe, including issuing protection notices for urupā, marae and biodiversity hotspots.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Create a Whenua Climate Restoration Fund giving iwi first right of refusal to buy back low-lying and coastal land, and a Māori Biodiversity Credit System (TTP-10)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says climate adaptation needs space and that iwi should control ecosystems that buffer against sea-level rise and food insecurity.

**How** (*archive*): A fund backing a compulsory first right of refusal for iwi to buy ecologically significant low-lying and coastal land, and Crown payments to whānau and iwi for carbon sequestration and ecosystem services from restored forests and wetlands.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Make marae official off-grid Civil Defence hubs with funded energy, water, stockpiles and training (TTP-11)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says marae already open their doors in emergencies long before state agencies arrive.

**How** (*archive*): Fund solar, batteries, rainwater collection and filtration at designated marae; stock emergency supplies and satellite communications; and legally designate marae as co-equal Civil Defence hubs under NEMA with funded emergency training for whānau.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Replace marine law with a Moana Ora Act protecting 30% of territorial waters through iwi/hapū-managed areas (TTP-12)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says current marine management is fragmented and ignores customary rights.

**How** (*archive*): Repeal and replace marine legislation with an act mandating Indigenous Protected and Conserved Areas, a binding 30% protection target co-designed and managed by iwi/hapū (including seasonal rāhui), an end to destructive bottom trawling and secured customary fishing rights.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Health

### Establish Te Aka Motuhake, a fully iwi-governed Māori health commissioning authority, plus a bonded iwi health scholarship scheme (TTP-05)

**Why** (*archive*): The party rejects the mainstreaming of indigenous health structures and wants to fix the Māori health workforce shortage.

**How** (*archive*): An autonomous, state-funded but iwi-governed health authority controlling clinical design, regional funding and provider licensing; an uncapped scholarship bonding graduates to Māori, iwi or rural providers for at least four years; and more diagnostic, preventative and dental services delivered from tribal hubs.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Housing

### Train local rangatahi to build hempcrete homes on papakāinga through a Rohe Construction Academy (TTP-08)

**Why** (*archive*): The party links overcrowded, damp housing to high rates of rheumatic fever and respiratory illness and says imported materials make building expensive.

**How** (*archive*): A funded trade academy in Te Tai Tokerau paying trainees a living wage; regional plants turning local hemp hurd and lime into certified building panels; and homes built on ancestral land and papakāinga, allocated first to overcrowded families and bypassing commercial developers.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Incomes & employment

### Wipe low-income whānau debt to MSD and IRD and replace the benefit system with a Universal Whānau Allowance (TTP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says whānau cannot retrain or innovate while being penalised by MSD, and that the current system creates a poverty trap.

**How** (*archive*): An immediate amnesty on about $2 billion of debt owed by low-income whānau to MSD and IRD; a simplified, non-taxable Universal Whānau Allowance for people in training or caregiving; and an end to 'relationship status' policing in the benefit system.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Fund 'Backyard Sovereignty Kits' (garden beds, chickens, rain tanks) and deregulate small-scale local food trade (TTP-06)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says supermarket prices are crippling for Northland whānau and that home food production should be treated as regional infrastructure.

**How** (*archive*): Funded flat-pack kits with raised beds, soil, seeds, a predator-proof coop and laying hens; rain-water catchment and irrigation; mobile gardening mentors; and an exemption of hyper-local household food barter and sales from council licensing and transaction taxes.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Fund community-owned Kai Sovereignty food hubs and require Northland supermarkets to give 30% of shelf space to local produce (TTP-21)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the supermarket duopoly trucks northern produce to Auckland and back with large markups.

**How** (*archive*): Fund regional processing hubs (kitchens, cold storage, butchery, packing), support direct-to-consumer networks, and require supermarkets in Te Tai Tokerau to allocate at least 30% of shelf space to locally grown unprocessed food bought from regional suppliers.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Law, justice & government

### Adopt a 'prison sinking lid' that diverts non-violent offenders with addiction or mental-health needs into hapū-run rehabilitation (TTP-04)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says each prisoner costs over $150,000 a year while reoffending stays high, and that rural communities lack preventative resources.

**How** (*archive*): Corrections savings from each bed vacated through health-focused diversion would be legally transferred to local hapū-led rehabilitation trusts running secure, alcohol- and drug-free 'healing sanctuaries', with mandatory restorative work programmes for those diverted.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Pass a Māori Justice & Autonomous Policing Act transferring youth-justice funding to iwi-governed authorities (TTP-18)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says state-controlled corrections and punitive policing entrench institutional inequity.

**How** (*archive*): Transfer regional youth-justice budgets to iwi-governed, marae-anchored authorities and fund iwi-administered community safety services under tribal jurisdiction, with restorative justice replacing incarceration.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Te ao Māori

### Create a Crown–Iwi Investment Fund and give mana whenua a 25% equity stake in major regional infrastructure (TTP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says the state should co-invest in iwi- and hapū-owned assets so whānau become owners in the value chain rather than low-wage labour.

**How** (*archive*): A Crown–Iwi Investment Fund for 'transition infrastructure' (renewable energy, green hydrogen, digital); major regional projects such as wind farms would have to offer at least 25% equity to local mana whenua, funded by low-interest government loans.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Constitutionally protect He Whakaputanga and Te Tiriti, and repeal the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 and the Treaty Clauses Review (TTP-13)

**Why** (*archive*): The party notes that both founding documents were signed in Te Tai Tokerau and wants protection against legislative harm to them.

**How** (*archive*): Advance a Tiriti-centred constitution led by community voices, and, as a priority, vote to repeal the Regulatory Standards Act 2025 and the Treaty Clauses Review.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Increase and entrench Waitangi Tribunal funding and make its findings binding on the Crown beyond specific land types (TTP-14)

**Why** (*archive*): The party sees the Tribunal as a forum for justice relied on by whānau.

**How** (*archive*): Raise and entrench funding (amount to be set after talks with the Tribunal and whānau) and extend the Tribunal's binding jurisdiction over the Crown.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Fund tangata whenua-led Te Tiriti education in the curriculum, the public service and for all MPs (TTP-15)

**How** (*archive*): More funding for Te Tiriti education led by tangata whenua, embedded in the NZ Curriculum and in public-service professional development, including for all sitting MPs.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Redirect 20% of Crown revenue from conservation and public land into a Māori-governed land-buyback fund (TTP-16)

**Why** (*archive*): The party wants to replace lengthy land-return negotiations with automatic, revenue-backed mechanisms.

**How** (*archive*): Legislate a mandatory 20% redirection of Crown revenues from conservation and public lands into a Māori-governed Land Acquisition Fund, remove LINZ's disposal authority and automatically return unused public-works land to its original owners, with a right of first refusal to buy back private land.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

### Create Te Whare Tohu Tātai, an independent Māori data and Crown-compliance commission (TTP-17)

**How** (*archive*): A statutory commission to monitor Crown compliance with all historical settlements, with ownership and control of all state data about Māori whānau and enforcement powers.

Full text: [TTP Pātaka Policy (Our Policies)](documents/ttp-pataka-policy.md) ([original](https://tetaitokerauparty.org.nz/our-policies/))

## Source documents

# Vision NZ (Vision New Zealand) — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Vision NZ (Vision New Zealand)** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **35 policies** listed, backed by **1 full-text source document**.

- Party website: <https://www.vision.org.nz/>
- Registration: 4 December 2019 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

Vision NZ, led by Hannah Tamaki, publishes its platform on a single "Our Policies" page in nine sections, each with a list of "Policy Commitments" followed by a policy overview. Every listed commitment is entered below as a separate policy (the "Why" lines paraphrase the section overview).

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/vision-nz/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** No costings, PDFs or fuller policy documents were found on vision.org.nz. The page gives no amounts for the weekly 'Family Empowerment Grant 2' or the newborn birth payment.

## Headline policies

- [Create a Ministry for Families](#create-a-ministry-for-families-vis-01) — Community & inclusion
- [Make the first $25,000 of personal income tax-free](#make-the-first-25000-of-personal-income-tax-free-vis-10) — Incomes & employment
- [Remove gender theory, Relationships and Sexuality Education and 'political propaganda' from the curriculum](#remove-gender-theory-relationships-and-sexuality-education-and-political-propaganda-from-the-curriculum-vis-15) — Education
- [Pause mass immigration immediately while visa policy is reviewed](#pause-mass-immigration-immediately-while-visa-policy-is-reviewed-vis-24) — Migration
- [Abolish MMP party lists so only electorate winners sit in Parliament, and cut the number of MPs](#abolish-mmp-party-lists-so-only-electorate-winners-sit-in-parliament-and-cut-the-number-of-mps-vis-34) — Law, justice & government

## Contents by topic

- [Community & inclusion](#community--inclusion) (6)
- [Defence & foreign affairs](#defence--foreign-affairs) (1)
- [Education](#education) (5)
- [Health](#health) (4)
- [Housing](#housing) (1)
- [Incomes & employment](#incomes--employment) (10)
- [Law, justice & government](#law-justice--government) (4)
- [Migration](#migration) (2)
- [Te ao Māori](#te-ao-māori) (1)
- [Transport & infrastructure](#transport--infrastructure) (1)

## Community & inclusion

### Create a Ministry for Families (VIS-01)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says the family is the cornerstone of society and that state agencies and regulation have eroded parents' confidence and authority.

**How** (*archive*): A dedicated ministry to act as a watchdog against state over-reach and promote solutions for households.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Reverse policies that override parents' rights, responsibilities, knowledge or consent (VIS-02)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says the family is the cornerstone of society and that state agencies and regulation have eroded parents' confidence and authority.

**How** (*archive*): Protect the 'nuclear family' by reversing such policies (the page does not list which).

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Set up a free 0800 helpline and put hapū liaison staff in every Oranga Tamariki office (VIS-08)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says the family is the cornerstone of society and that state agencies and regulation have eroded parents' confidence and authority.

**How** (*archive*): Aimed at stopping 'forced state interventions' in families.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Adopt 'One Nation, One People, One Vote, One Government, One Flag, Under One God' as a unifying principle (VIS-23)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says it stands for one unified country free of 'global overreach' and race-based politics.

**How** (*archive*): Stated as the party's core principle.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Declare English the official language of New Zealand (VIS-27)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says it stands for one unified country free of 'global overreach' and race-based politics.

**How** (*archive*): Make English the official language.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Define sex in law strictly as male and female and designate single-sex spaces and women's sport by biological sex (VIS-29)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says biological sex should be upheld in law to protect women's privacy, safety and rights, and to protect children.

**How** (*archive*): Legal definition of biological sex; toilets, changing rooms, refuges and prisons designated by sex; sport categories restricted by biological sex; review the Births, Deaths, Marriages and Relationships Registration Act 2021.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

## Defence & foreign affairs

### Leave the United Nations and the Paris Agreement (VIS-25)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says it stands for one unified country free of 'global overreach' and race-based politics.

**How** (*archive*): To 'restore absolute national sovereignty'.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

## Education

### Remove gender theory, Relationships and Sexuality Education and 'political propaganda' from the curriculum (VIS-15)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says education standards have declined because schools shifted from core academics to 'social engineering'.

**How** (*archive*): Remove these from the national curriculum after an independent review for political bias.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Refocus schools on a knowledge-rich curriculum of literacy, numeracy, science and 'balanced history' (VIS-16)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says education standards have declined because schools shifted from core academics to 'social engineering'.

**How** (*archive*): Centre the curriculum 'strictly' on those subjects.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Invest heavily in early childhood education focused on language, literacy and social skills (VIS-17)

**Why** (*archive*): Vision NZ says education standards have declined because schools shifted from core academics to 'social engineering'.

**How** (*archive*): High-quality ECE investment, and keep ECE free of 'inappropriate ideological, foreign religious, or overt cultural content'.

Full text: [Vision NZ — Our Policies](documents/vision-policies.md) ([original](https://www.vision.org.nz/visionpolicies))

### Raise teacher salaries and cut their administrative workload (VIS-18)

# Women's Rights Party — 2026 election policies

Every policy of **Women's Rights Party** for the 7 November 2026 general election that this archive could find: **17 policies** listed, backed by **16 full-text source documents**.

- Party website: <https://womensrightsparty.nz/>
- Registration: 28 August 2023 (Electoral Commission register)

## About this list

The Women's Rights Party, a sex-based-rights feminist party, publishes 13 'policy proposal' pages (each with a Proposal and Rationale), an 'Our Priorities' page and a downloadable full policy document (Word file dated 4 Nov 2025, which also contains members' policy-amendment proposals). Each distinct policy is listed below.

**Method.** Pages and PDFs were downloaded on 2026-10-23 by [`tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_sites_fetch.py) / [`tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_opportunity_fetch.py) (raw copies in `raw/party-docs/womens-rights/`) and reduced to their main text in [`documents/`](documents/) (markup and whitespace normalised only). The list and summaries are built by [`tools/policies_minor_build.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_build.py) from [`tools/policies_minor_catalog.py`](../../../tools/policies_minor_catalog.py).

policy.nz publishes no policy statements for this party, so every summary here is marked *archive*: written for this archive from the linked full text in one to three neutral sentences ("Why" = the party's own stated reason, attributed; "How" = what it says it would do). Party claims (costs, statistics) are reported as the party's claims, not verified.

**Gaps and caveats.** The full policy document is a Word file converted with pandoc; its proposal forms are tables, kept as HTML tables. No 2026-specific manifesto or costings were found; the web policy pages are undated.

## Headline policies

- [Ban puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones for under-18s with 'sex-related distress' and restrict funded gender surgery to over-25s](#ban-puberty-blockers-and-cross-sex-hormones-for-under-18s-with-sex-related-distress-and-restrict-funded-gender-surgery-to-over-25s-wrp-01) — Health

## Community & inclusion

### Record biological sex on birth certificates and repeal sex self-identification (WRP-02)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says women's rights must be based on biological sex rather than gender identity.

**How** (*archive*): Amend the Births, Deaths, Marriages and Relationships Registration Act 2021 to remove 'nominated sex'; sex could be corrected only if originally recorded wrongly (e.g. undetected DSD).

Full text: [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

### Oppose adding 'gender identity and gender expression' to the Human Rights Act (WRP-03)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says it could undermine sex-based exceptions.

Full text: [POLICY – Human Rights Act – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-human-rights-act.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/human-rights-act/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

**Why** (*archive*): It supports protecting lesbian, gay and bisexual people from conversion practices but says 'gender' is not a clear concept for law.

Full text: [Conversion Practices – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-conversion-practices.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/conversion-practices/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

**Why** (*archive*): The party says surrogacy cannot be free of exploitation and having a baby by surrogacy is not a human right.

**How** (*archive*): Keep the birth mother as first legal parent with longer than seven days to decide; children should be able to learn their origins.

Full text: [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

**Why** (*archive*): The party says women's rights must be based on biological sex rather than gender identity.

**How** (*archive*): Single-sex toilets, changing rooms, refuges, wards, sports and women-only groups (including online); school privacy from the opposite sex; supportive conditions for pregnant prisoners and mothers.

Full text: [Protecting Women’s and Children’s Spaces and Safety – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-se.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-services-to-support-detransitioners/)); [Women's Rights Party Full Policy (Word document, 4 Nov 2025)](documents/full-policy-docx-2025.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/POLICY-Womens-Rights-Party-2025-041125.docx))

**How** (*archive*): More resources to leave domestic violence and accessible, affordable, enforced protection orders.

Full text: [Protecting Women’s and Children’s Spaces and Safety – Women's Rights Party](documents/proposal-exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-se.md) ([original](https://womensrightsparty.nz/policy-proposal/exit-services-for-women-leaving-gangs-religious-cults-and-services-to-support-detransitioners/))

### Use language in law, health and education that defines women as adult human females and motherhood as exclusively female (WRP-17)

**Why** (*archive*): The party says women's rights must be based on biological sex rather than gender identity.

**How** (*archive*): Keep words such as 'mother', 'woman' and 'breastfeeding' in maternity services.

guide/issues.md: # The big issues: where the parties stand (2026 election) *Information as at **2026-10-23**. Built from [`data/guide/issues.json`](../data/guide/issues.json) by `tools/guide_render.py`; see also the [party guide](parties.md).* Issues were chosen from what voters say matters most in the 2026 Ipsos Issues Monitor surveys (cost of living, healthcare, the economy, unemployment, housing, fuel prices, poverty, crime, climate, education, with tax rising) plus the areas where party platforms differ most. For each issue: why it matters, a few sourced facts, and a one- or two-sentence summary of each party's published 2026 policy. A party is left out of an issue when we found no 2026 position on it. Summaries describe what parties propose, not whether it would work. ## Issues - 👛 [Cost of living](#cost-of-living) - ❤️ [Health](#health) - 💼 [Economy and jobs](#economy-and-jobs) - 🏠 [Housing and rent](#housing-and-rent) - 🪙 [Tax](#tax) - ⚡ [Power bills and fuel prices](#energy-and-fuel) - 🤝 [Welfare and poverty](#welfare-and-poverty) - 🛡️ [Law and order](#law-and-order) - 🌿 [Climate and environment](#climate-and-environment) - 📚 [Schools and education](#education) - 🪶 [Te Tiriti o Waitangi and Māori issues](#te-tiriti-and-maori-issues) - 🛣️ [Infrastructure and transport](#infrastructure-and-transport) - ✈️ [Immigration](#immigration) - ⏳ [Superannuation and retirement](#superannuation-and-retirement) - 🚜 [Farming and rural New Zealand](#agriculture-and-rural) - 🌏 [Foreign affairs, trade and defence](#foreign-affairs-and-defence) - 🗳️ [Democracy and how government works](#democracy-and-government) --- ## 👛 Cost of living **Why it matters:** Prices for things like petrol, power and food have been rising faster than the Reserve Bank's 1-3% target. It is the number one worry for voters this year. Parties disagree on whether the answer is more competition, tax changes or direct help with bills. **Key facts:** - Prices rose 3.7% in the year to the September 2026 quarter (down from 4.1% in June), above the Reserve Bank's 1-3% target. ([stats.govt.nz](https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/consumers-price-index-september-2026-quarter/), [interest.co.nz](https://www.interest.co.nz/economy/140742/annual-inflation-hits-37-september-quarter-petrol-continuing-lead-way-followed)) - Petrol was the biggest driver, up 19.1% on a year earlier in the CPI; electricity was up 9.3% and council rates 6.2%. ([interest.co.nz](https://www.interest.co.nz/economy/140742/annual-inflation-hits-37-september-quarter-petrol-continuing-lead-way-followed)) - Food prices rose 2.4% in the year to September 2026. # "Find your match" quiz: how it works

The quiz data is in [`data/guide/quiz.json`](../data/guide/quiz.json). It is built by `tools/quiz_build.py` from the hand-checked records in `tools/quiz_data.py`. The quiz works like Vote Compass or the policy.nz matcher. You rate statements from "strongly disagree" to "strongly agree", and the quiz shows how close each party's **public record** is to your answers.

It is a conversation starter, not a voting instruction. Read the parties' own policies (see `parties/<party>/policies/`) before you decide.

## 1. How the statements were chosen

We picked 45 statements. Each one had to meet four tests:

1. **It is a real 2026 dividing line.** At least two parties take clearly different public positions on it, or a recent law or vote split Parliament. Statements that every party agrees with (for example "Pharmac should get more money") were left out.
2. **It is concrete.** Where possible it names a specific mechanism, such as a 28% capital gains tax, the Fast-track Approvals Act, the Regulatory Standards Act, an age of 65 or 2% of GDP. Vague aims like "a fairer economy" were not used.
3. **It is neutrally worded.** Each statement is a plain proposal that a reasonable person could agree or disagree with. Where possible the wording avoids party names and loaded terms. Some statements say "should" and others propose reversing a change, to limit "agree-bias".
4. **It is spread across the main issues.** The issues are tax, cost of living, work, housing, health, education, crime and justice, climate, environment, energy, Te Tiriti and co-governance, democracy, local government, immigration, superannuation, welfare, transport, agriculture, foreign policy, defence, drugs and social issues.

Every statement has a one-sentence `explainer` giving neutral background.

## 2. How party positions were recorded

Each cell is `{position, evidence, source_url, policy_id?}` or `null`.

| Score | Meaning | When we used it |
|---:|---|---|
| +2 | Strongly agree | Explicit policy commitment, a "Yes" survey answer, or voting for the measure |
| +1 | Agree | Supports the direction with a material qualification, or a weaker version |
| 0 | Mixed or neutral | The party said it would neither push for nor oppose it, or its statements conflict (e.g. voted one way and later said the opposite) |
| −1 | Disagree | Opposes the direction with qualifications, or has a stated contrary approach |
| −2 | Strongly disagree | Explicit opposition, a "No" survey answer, or voting against the measure |
| `null` | No position found | Absence of evidence. **This is not a guess, and it does not count as neutral.** |

The rules we followed:

- **We never guess.** If we could not find a public statement, vote, policy document or survey answer, the cell is `null`. Where a party has said nothing, we did not infer a position from its general philosophy (for example "lower taxes" does not count as opposing a wealth tax).
- **A survey answer of "No change" is not counted as opposition.** It only means the party has not proposed the policy, so those cells are `null`.
- **Evidence is a short quote or close paraphrase.** Each cell has a `source_url` for the party page, PDF, Hansard-based record, survey answer or news report. When the cell matches a policy.nz statement, its id (e.g. `POL54670`) is in `policy_id`, so the full policy.nz summary and citations can be shown.
- **Sources, in order of preference:**
  1. Party policy documents and releases. These are archived verbatim under `parties/*/policies/documents/`, and the policy.nz dataset is in `raw/policy.nz/parties/*.json`.
  2. Recorded parliamentary votes on the relevant bill: Treaty Principles Bill second reading (10 Apr 2025), Regulatory Standards Bill, Fast-track Approvals Act, the reinstated three-strikes law and the Crown Minerals Amendment Act 2025.
  3. Party answers to 2026 election questionnaires: Greenpeace's environmental scorecard methodology, which quotes party answers in full; NZCTU's worker scorecards; and Grey Power's superannuation questionnaire.
  4. The KPMG 2026 tax policy tracker, and reputable news (RNZ, 1News, ODT, Te Ao Māori News).
- **Where we relied on a third party's assessment rather than the party's own words, the evidence says so.** For example, "Greenpeace assessment" is used where National and ACT did not answer and Greenpeace scored them from their voting record. Older statements are dated in the evidence text, such as Te Pāti Māori's May 2023 superannuation position.
- **Votes and policies can point different ways.** For example, NZ First voted for the Regulatory Standards Act and later said it would repeal it. We record this as 0 and explain it in the evidence.

Downloaded source material used only for the quiz is in `raw/quiz/`. It includes the KPMG tracker, the Greenpeace methodology, NZCTU scorecards, Grey Power responses, Alliance PDFs and the cached pages and Wikipedia extracts we checked.

## 3. Suggested scoring method

For each statement *i* that **both** the user and the party answered:

```
agreement_i = 1 − |user_i − party_i| / 4          (1 = identical, 0 = opposite ends)
```

The user can set an importance weight *w_i* for each statement: 0.5 for "less important", 1 for "normal" (the default) and 2 for "very important". A user can also skip a statement.

```
raw_match = Σ w_i · agreement_i / Σ w_i            (over statements both answered)
```

**Correcting for coverage.** A party with only two recorded positions could score 100% by luck. To stop thin records being over-rewarded, we shrink each party's score toward the neutral 0.5 by a few "phantom" neutral statements (k = 3):

```
match = (Σ w_i · agreement_i + k · 0.5) / (Σ w_i + k)
```

**What to show the user** for each party:

- the match % (adjusted);
- **coverage**, meaning "based on N of your M answers";
- a "limited information" badge when N < 10;
- the per-statement breakdown with each party's evidence quote and source link.

Parties should be ranked by the adjusted match. The raw match can be shown on request.

A worked example: a user answers 40 statements. Party A has positions on 35 of them, with a raw match of 0.70 and an adjusted match of (35·0.70 + 1.5)/(35 + 3) = 0.68. Party B has positions on 2, with a raw match of 1.00 and an adjusted match of (2 + 1.5)/5 = 0.70. Party B would still rank close to the top, but it would carry the "based on 2 of your 40 answers" badge.

Using no shrinkage at all (k = 0) is reasonable if coverage is shown very prominently. We suggest a k between 3 and 5.

## 4. Limitations

- **Coverage is uneven.** The seven parties covered by policy.nz have far more positions recorded than the ten smaller parties. Many small parties publish only a few single-issue policies, so their match scores are much less reliable.
- **Positions are a snapshot as of 23 October 2026.** Parties are still releasing policy before the 7 November election. National, for example, had not released a detailed superannuation policy, and Labour said its full manifesto was still to come.
- **The 5-point coding involves judgement.** Choosing between +1 and +2 or between −1 and −2 is a judgement call. We applied the same rules to every party, and the evidence for every cell is shown so readers can check it.
- **Third-party scorecards have their own framing.** The Greenpeace and NZCTU questions are advocacy-group questions. We only used the party's own answer, or the voting-record evidence cited, and not the group's grade.
- **Votes are not always policy.** Voting against a bill does not always mean a party would repeal the law. Where a party has said what it would do, that statement is used ahead of the vote.
- **Conscience issues are mostly `null`.** Most parties have no party line on issues such as abortion and cannabis, so most cells for those statements are `null`.
- **Matching on policies is not the whole picture.** The quiz ignores competence, record in government, coalition options and which party is likely to deliver. The track-record files in `parties/<party>/track-record.md` cover some of this.
- **Statement selection shapes the results.** Different statements would give different matches. We aimed for a broad and balanced set, but no set is neutral.

```
python3 -I tools/quiz_fetch_text.py <url> [regex]         # fetch and cache a news page into raw/quiz/pages
python3 -I tools/quiz_wiki.py "<Wikipedia title>" [regex] # bill and vote records
```

To add or correct a position, edit `tools/quiz_data.py` and rebuild. The builder refuses any cell that has no evidence or no source, any `policy_id` that is unknown or belongs to a different party, and any party slug that is not in the list.

# 2026 electorates — voter guide

New Zealand votes on **Saturday 7 November 2026**. You get two votes: a **party vote** (decides how many seats each party gets) and an **electorate vote** for your local MP. There are **71 electorates** in 2026 — 64 general (48 North Island, 16 South Island) and 7 Māori — one fewer than in 2023 after the 2025 boundary review.

Find your electorate: [Electoral Commission electorate maps](https://elections.nz/democracy-in-nz/historical-events/boundary-review-2025/electorate-maps) · [interactive map](https://elections.nz/maps/boundary-review-2025). Data: [`data/electorates/2026.json`](../data/electorates/2026.json).

## What changed in the 2025 boundary review

The Representation Commission finalised boundaries on 8 August 2025: 19 electorates were unchanged and the boundaries of 49 general and three Māori electorates were adjusted, mainly in Auckland, Bay of Plenty, Christchurch and the lower North Island, where one North Island general seat was removed ([Electoral Commission](https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2025/electorate-boundaries-finalised); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_New_Zealand_general_election)).

| New / renamed 2026 seat | Status | Predecessor seat(s) |

| [East Cape](east-cape.md) | renamed | East Coast |
| [Glendene](glendene.md) | new | Kelston, Te Atatū, New Lynn |
| [Henderson](henderson.md) | new | Te Atatū, Upper Harbour, Kaipara ki Mahurangi |
| [Kapiti](kapiti.md) | new | Ōtaki, Mana |
| [Kenepuru](kenepuru.md) | new | Mana, Ōhāriu |
| [Mt Maunganui](mt-maunganui.md) | renamed | Bay of Plenty, Tauranga |
| [Ōtāhuhu](otahuhu.md) | renamed | Panmure-Ōtāhuhu |
| [Tauranga](tauranga.md) | reconfigured | Tauranga, Bay of Plenty |
| [Waitākere](waitakere.md) | new | New Lynn, Kelston |
| [Wellington Bays](wellington-bays.md) | renamed | Rongotai, Wellington Central |
| [Wellington North](wellington-north.md) | renamed | Wellington Central, Ōhāriu |

**Abolished or renamed 2023 seats:** Bay of Plenty (renamed Mt Maunganui); East Coast (renamed East Cape); Kelston (split into Glendene and Waitākere); New Lynn (split into Waitākere (and a small part to Glendene)); Te Atatū (split into Henderson and Glendene); Panmure-Ōtāhuhu (became Ōtāhuhu (Panmure moved out)); Mana (split between Kenepuru and Kapiti); Ōtaki (replaced by Kapiti); Ōhāriu (split mainly between Kenepuru and Wellington North); Wellington Central (renamed Wellington North (Mount Cook/Brooklyn to Wellington Bays)); Rongotai (renamed Wellington Bays).

# Auckland Central electorate (general)

**Region:** Auckland  
**Election day:** Saturday 7 November 2026  
**Boundary status:** continuing (same name; boundaries may have been adjusted in the 2025 review)

## About this electorate

Auckland Central covers Auckland’s city centre, suburbs such as Ponsonby, Newton and Arch Hill, as well as the islands of the Hauraki Gulf. It is currently held by Green party co-leader Chlöe Swabrick, who won the electorate with a margin of 16,624 votes and has held the seat since 2020. National won the party vote in 2023 with 33%, followed by the Green Party on 24%. Barring one three year gap, the seat was held continuously by Labour from 1919-2008, but it has not regained it since.

_Description quoted from [policy.nz](https://policy.nz/2026/auckland-central-electorate)._

**Fact-check notes on the description above** (checked against official 2023 results):

- "margin of 16,624" (that figure is the winner’s vote total) — the official 2023 majority was 3,896 votes over Mahesh Muralidhar.

Resigned from Parliament in June 2014 after a High Court conviction for filing a false electoral return, which was later overturned; in May 2015 the Court of Appeal declined to order a retrial after new evidence showed Kim and Mona Dotcom's account had been fabricated. Not a 2026 candidate. ## Biography Born in Wellington on 2 December 1946; his parents were imprisoned for procuring abortions when he was a child and from age two he was raised by an aunt and uncle among many foster children, later attending Avondale College. Worked in pharmaceutical market research, commercial property development and restaurants. Birkenhead Borough councillor from 1977. Married Amanda Medcalf in 1987 (later separated); they adopted three children from St Petersburg. CNZM (2011), QSO (2000). A long-time talkback host (Radio Pacific 1992–2007; later MagicTalk). ## Political career - National MP for Whangarei 1981–1999; Minister of Police, Tourism and Sport from 1990; left Cabinet in 1996 rather than serve alongside coalition partner Winston Peters; retired in 1999. - Mayor of Auckland City 2001–2004 (lost to Dick Hubbard) and 2007–2010; lost the 2010 Auckland "super city" mayoralty to Len Brown. - Joined ACT in May 2011 and won **Epsom** in 2011 (after the "cup of tea" with John Key) as ACT's only MP; ACT leader from February 2012 to 2014 (succeeded by Jamie Whyte, who was not an MP). Minister outside Cabinet in John Key's government until resigning his portfolios in October 2013 when committed for trial. ## Record & notable actions - As a 1990s minister he said he could not persuade Cabinet to ban semi-automatic guns after Aramoana; after the 2019 Christchurch attacks he said he was "haunted" by that. - As ACT leader secured, under the 2011 confidence-and-supply deal, the introduction of partnership (charter) schools. - Voted for the 2013 marriage equality law, saying that "if I knew then what I have since learnt, I would have acted differently" — reversing his 1986 opposition to homosexual law reform. - The Local Electoral Amendment Act 2013 (the "John Banks bill") tightened rules on anonymous local-election donations in response to his 2010 return. ## Controversies - **False electoral return (2010–2015):** charged by private prosecution over two $25,000 donations from Kim Dotcom declared as anonymous; convicted on 1 August 2014 (two months' community detention), conviction quashed on appeal in November 2014, and no retrial ordered in May 2015. - Long record of contentious remarks: opposing 1986 homosexual law reform ("sad and sickening day"), comments about Asian immigrants (2004) and Māori men in a safe-sex campaign (2006); in January 2021 MagicTalk dropped him after he agreed on air with a caller that Māori were a "stone age" people. - The 2011 "teapot tape" — a journalist's recording of his private conversation with John Key — became a major election-campaign controversy. - In a 2016 paternity case brought by Antony Shaw, the High Court declared Banks to be Shaw's birth father; Shaw's mother alleged in an affidavit that Banks had pressured her to take drugs to induce a miscarriage in 1969, which Banks had denied. ## Sources - https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=John_Banks_(New_Zealand_politician)&oldid=1347319196 - http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11268295 - http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11393301 - https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1304/S00335/speech-john-banks-on-voting-for-marriage-amendment-bill.htm - https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/christchurch-shooting/111644333/haunted-john-banks-says-semiautomatic-weapons-should-have-been-banned-in-1990 - http://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2013/0040/27.0/DLM4803506.html

Standing in **Pakuranga** and **#10** on ACT's list for 2026. ## Biography Born in India in 1970, the daughter of an Indian Air Force officer; master's in biochemistry in India, moved to New Zealand in 1995 and gained a PhD in biological sciences from the University of Auckland (2003). Worked as a scientist, co-directed a confectionery company and hosted current-affairs talkback on Radio Tarana; served on the Film and Video Labelling Body and the Families Commission board. The first Indian-born woman to represent a party in the New Zealand Parliament. ## Political career - National candidate for Mount Roskill in 2014, the 2016 by-election and 2017 (second each time); National list MP 2014–2020; lost in 2020 and was not selected by National for 2023. - Switched to ACT on 31 May 2023; ACT candidate for Pakuranga (third) and elected at list #9. ## Record & notable actions - As a National MP: Newborn Enrolment with General Practice Bill (passed first reading unanimously in 2017, defeated at second reading 2018); Patents (Advancement Patents) Amendment Bill (defeated 2018); a private bill fixing Auckland Regional Amenities funding reporting (law July 2020). - As ACT education spokesperson opposed University of Auckland Māori and Pasifika "safe spaces" (2024) and its compulsory Waipapa Taumata Rau course (2025); introduced a member's bill (March 2025) to bar universities offering ethnicity-based services including scholarships and accommodation. - In June 2026 asked the Police Commissioner to investigate Brian Tamaki's remarks about purging non-Christians. ## Controversies - In 2014 Labour's Rajen Prasad questioned her remaining on the Families Commission board after she was photographed wearing a National rosette; she resigned on being confirmed as a candidate. - In April 2026 she was the target of a haka by former Te Pāti Māori president Che Wilson at a regional kapa haka competition that included the phrase "bloody Indian curry" and mocked Indian accents; she called it "deeply troubling". Te Matatini and Whakaata Māori removed the footage, and several Māori commentators condemned the performance while also criticising ACT's policies. ## 2026 candidacy - **Electorate:** Pakuranga - **List ranking:** 10 - **Before politics:** Business owner - **Residence:** Auckland - **Age:** 56 - **Public email:** parmjeet.parmar@parliament.govt.nz - **Website:** https://www.act.org.nz/people/parmjeet-parmar - **Facebook:** https://www.facebook.com/DrParmjeetParmar - **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/parmjeet.parmar.77/ - **Twitter:** https://x.com/Parmjeet_Parmar _Source: candidate questionnaire answers published on [policy.nz](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party), retrieved Oct 2026._ ## Sources - https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Parmjeet_Parmar&oldid=1380810712 - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_lists_in_the_2026_New_Zealand_general_election - https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/parmar-parmjeet - https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-proposed-laws/document/BILL_74075/newborn-enrolment-with-general-practice-bill - http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11756320 - http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/9818868/Families-Commission-questioned-over-political-links - https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party

ACT candidate at **#4** on the party list for the 7 November 2026 election — a position likely to win a seat if ACT polls near its 2023 level. ## Biography Born Paul Henry Hopes in Auckland on 4 August 1960; moved to Bristol with his mother at 11. Began at the BBC, then worked on National Radio, 2ZD Wairarapa and his own Today FM (1991–92), Radio Pacific and Radio Live. Co-hosted TVNZ's *Breakfast* (2004–2010), Network Ten's *Breakfast* in Sydney (2012), *The Paul Henry Show* (2014) and *Paul Henry* on TV3/Radio Live (2015–2016), then semi-retired; later host of *The Traitors NZ* and *The Chase NZ*. Author of *What Was I Thinking* (2011) and *Outraged* (2013). Appointed to the TVNZ board in 2025. ## Political career - National candidate for Wairarapa in 1999. - Spoke at ACT's 2024 "Change Makers" event, calling ACT "the last cab left on the rank heading in the right direction"; announced as an ACT candidate in 2026. ## Controversies - Resigned from TVNZ in 2010 after mocking the name of Indian politician Sheila Dikshit and questioning whether Governor-General Sir Anand Satyanand "looks and sounds like a New Zealander"; New Zealand's government apologised to India. - In July 2026 said on Radio Hauraki, in a "shoot, shag or marry" game, that he would "shoot" Labour leader Chris Hipkins; Hipkins and Ayesha Verrall called it offensive and akin to a death threat, Henry called it "manufactured outrage", and David Seymour and Nicole McKee defended it as a risqué game. ## 2026 candidacy - **List ranking:** 4 - **Before politics:** Broadcaster - **Residence:** Auckland - **Age:** 66 - **Public email:** paul.henry@act.org.nz - **Website:** https://www.act.org.nz/people/paul-henry - **Facebook:** https://www.facebook.com/paulhenryact - **Instagram:** https://www.instagram.com/thehenryspirit/ - **Twitter:** https://x.com/actparty ### Current role Not currently in parliament ### Year entered parliament Not previously in parliament ### Why I'm standing New Zealand should be one of the most prosperous countries on Earth, but we're not meeting our potential. My wife and I have ten grandchildren between us, and I want them to inherit a country that rewards hard work, values freedom, and gives people the opportunity to build better lives. I'm running because I'm not prepared to sit back while New Zealand becomes poorer, less ambitious, and weighed down by ever-bigger government. Party vote ACT. ### About me I've spent decades asking difficult questions, challenging people in power, and saying what I think. I'll bring energy and common-sense to Parliament. I'm standing list-only. The best way to elect me and more of ACT's strong team is to party vote ACT. It'll keep the coalition Government in power, but going further and faster on the issues that matter most. This election is crucial, a lurch to the left would devastate our economy for generations. _Source: candidate questionnaire answers published on [policy.nz](https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party), retrieved Oct 2026._ ## Sources - https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paul_Henry_(broadcaster)&oldid=1377442055 - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_lists_in_the_2026_New_Zealand_general_election - https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/776520/shoot-shag-or-marry-game-was-act-candidate-paul-henry-being-authentic-seymour-says - https://policy.nz/2026/party-vote/parties/act-party

Worked as a civil and environmental engineer for Auckland City Council and ran his own engineering firm. While working for MWH Global in Fiji (2016–17) he was deported after the firm's dispute with the Fiji Roads Authority; he says it followed his criticism of Chinese contractors' workmanship. Not a 2026 candidate. ## Biography Born in Auckland in 1958 and educated at St Cuthbert's College and the University of Auckland (arts and law). She worked as a communications officer for the New Zealand Forest Service on the West Coast, then from 1984 to 1990 at Parliament as a Labour research officer and press secretary to Helen Clark. After moving to Christchurch she was a freelance journalist and, from 1993 to 2007, a field officer and spokesperson for Forest & Bird, campaigning on the environmental impacts of logging, mining and dairying. the elected council was replaced by government-appointed commissioners in 2010, which she said prompted her to run for Parliament. - Green list MP 2011–2023 (contested Selwyn 2011, Port Hills 2014 and 2017, Banks Peninsula 2020). - In the first term of the Sixth Labour Government (2017–2020) she was Minister of Conservation, Minister for Land Information and Associate Minister for the Environment (Greens' ministers outside Cabinet under the confidence-and-supply deal). - Chair of Parliament's Environment Committee 2020–2023. ## Record & notable actions - Led development of Te Mana o te Taiao, the Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy; after criticism (including from the Law Society) Labour removed it and the Greens withdrew support for the bill. - Voted for marriage equality (2013), the End of Life Choice Act (2019) and the Abortion Legislation Act (2020). ## Controversies - Her Himalayan tahr cull plan (2019–20) drew strong opposition from hunters, led to death threats against her, and was scaled back. - As Land Information Minister she was criticised by former Green MP Sue Bradford for approving "nearly every" overseas land-purchase application despite Green policy; Sage said the law gave her little discretion. # James Shaw | | | |---|---| | **Party (current/most recent)** | Green Party | | **Status** | Former MP | | **Party history** | Green Party (1990s–present) | | **Parliaments (50th–54th)** | 51, 52, 53, 54 | | **First elected** | 2014 | | **Key roles** | Green Party co-leader (2015–2024)

Associate Minister for the Environment (Biodiversity) (2020–2023) | | **Born** | 1973-05-06, Wellington | | **Wikipedia** | [James Shaw (New Zealand politician)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Shaw_(New_Zealand_politician)) | Photo: Supplied by the Green Party; uploader will deal with VRT — CC BY-SA 4.0 — [source](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:James_Shaw_2023_%28cropped%29.jpg) ## Current status Former MP and former Green co-leader. Stepped down as co-leader in March 2024 (succeeded by Chlöe Swarbrick) and left Parliament on 5 May 2024 (replaced by Francisco Hernandez). Now works in climate-related business and governance roles, including Morrison & Co. Not a 2026 candidate. ## Biography Born in Wellington on 6 May 1973 and raised mainly by his mother Cynthia Shaw and later also her partner Susanne Jungersen. Attended Wellington High School and Victoria University of Wellington, then spent 12 years in London, where he completed an MSc in sustainability and business leadership at the University of Bath (2005) and worked in PwC's consulting division. Returned to Wellington in 2010 and worked for HSBC on environmental-leadership programmes and at the Akina Foundation social enterprise. Married to Annabel; lives in Aro Valley. ## Political career - Volunteered for the Greens from 1990; stood for Wellington City Council at 19 (1992). - Green candidate in Wellington Central 2011, 2014, 2017 and 2020; list MP from 2014. - Elected male co-leader on 30 May 2015 after seven months as an MP, beating Kevin Hague (54% to 44% of first preferences). Sole leader through the 2017 campaign after Metiria Turei's resignation; co-leader with Marama Davidson from 2018. - Minister for Climate Change, Minister of Statistics and Associate Minister of Finance (outside Cabinet) from 2017 under the Labour–NZ First–Green arrangement; retained Climate Change and gained Associate Environment (Biodiversity) under the 2020 cooperation agreement. - Re-elected co-leader 116–4 against James Cockle (2021). Not reconfirmed in the July 2022 annual vote, triggering a contest; re-elected with 142 of 145 delegate votes (97%) on 10 September 2022. - Announced in January 2024 he would step down as co-leader; his Bill of Rights amendment adding a "right to a sustainable environment" was defeated at first reading on 10 April 2024. ## Record & notable actions - **Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Act 2019**: introduced by Shaw in May 2019, it set net-zero targets for long-lived gases by 2050, created the independent Climate Change Commission and a system of emissions budgets. It passed with near-unanimous support. - Backed the 2018 decision to end new offshore oil and gas exploration permits ("nuclear-free moment of our generation"). - Represented New Zealand at UN climate conferences (COP) during 2017–2023. - Described himself as part of a "pro-market" Green tradition that believes markets can be reformed to incorporate sustainability. ## Controversies - **Green School funding (2020):** approved $11.7 million from the COVID-19 "shovel-ready" fund for a private school in Taranaki, contrary to Green policy against state funding of private schools; criticised by teachers' unions, principals and former Green MPs. He apologised on 1 September 2020 calling it "an error of judgment"; the grant was later converted into a loan. Education Minister Chris Hipkins disputed Shaw's account that he had given verbal approval. - **2018 census**: as Statistics Minister he was criticised over the census's low response rate. - Criticised in 2018 for the highest ministerial international airfare spending in one quarter (NZ$77,771), which he attributed to climate conferences; and in 2021 for MIQ places allocated to his COP26 delegation. - On 14 March 2019 he was assaulted while walking to Parliament; a 47-year-old man was charged. (Shaw was the victim.) ## Sources - https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=James_Shaw_(New_Zealand_politician)&oldid=1359183916 - https://www.beehive.govt.nz/minister/biography/james-shaw - https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/shaw-james/ - http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11457327 - https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/515700/james-shaw-s-valedictory-and-his-new-roles - https://www.legislation.govt.nz/act/public/2019/0061/latest/whole.html

parties/independent/people/darleen-tana/: # Darleen Tana | | | |---|---| | **Party (current/most recent)** | Independent | | **Status** | Former MP | | **Party history** | Green Party (by 2020–2024-07-08); Independent (2024-07-08–2024-10-22) | | **Parliaments (50th–54th)** | 54 | | **First elected** | 2023 | | **Key roles** | Green spokesperson on oceans and fisheries, science, small business, media, internal affairs (Nov 2023 – Mar 2024) | | **Born** | Northland (year not published) | | **Wikipedia** | [Darleen Tana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darleen_Tana) | Photo: Schwede66 — CC BY-SA 4.0 — [source](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Darleen_Tana_%28cropped%29.jpg) ## Current status Former MP. Elected for the Greens in 2023, she resigned from the party on 8 July 2024 and sat as an independent until Speaker Gerry Brownlee declared her seat vacant on 22 October 2024 under the "waka-jumping" law, following a Green Party vote. Replaced by Benjamin Doyle. Not a 2026 candidate. ## Biography Darleen Sheree Tana Hoff-Nielsen was born in Northland and is of Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Porou, Ngā Rauru, Te Āti Awa and Ngāti Kahungunu ki Wairarapa descent. Educated at Bay of Islands College and Whangārei Girls' High School; Bachelor of Chemical Technology (Massey) and, on a Rotary scholarship, an MBA from Solvay Business School in Brussels, where she worked in telecommunications talent management. List MP 2023–2026. - Assistant Speaker (2017–2020), Deputy Speaker (2020–2022), and **Speaker of the House, 24 Aug 2022 – Dec 2023** — the second Māori Speaker after Sir Peter Tapsell ([RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/473418/gaurav-sharma-hijacks-speaker-ceremony-to-accuse-trevor-mallard)). - Opposition spokesperson for Whānau Ora and associate Māori development (2023–2026). ## Record & notable actions - His Official Information (Parliamentary Under-Secretaries) Amendment Bill, bringing under-secretaries under the OIA, became law in 2016 ([Parliament](https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-proposed-laws/document/00DBHOH_BILL64530_1/official-information-parliamentary-under-secretaries)). -
